1.title: DM sales assistant (Instagram, Telegram-alternatives, Bale, Eitaa)
1.verdict_md: Verdict: the unit economics work (gross margin about 77–81% after GPU and gateway), but the business is fixed-cost heavy, so it only breaks even at about 205 paying customers. In the base case that happens in month 14, with peak cash need of about 2.7 billion toman (about $10,100). Tags: \[S\] sourced, \[D\] derived from tagged inputs (recomputed by code), \[A\] assumption.

sections_md.canvas:
| Block | Content |
| --- | --- |
| Customer segments | (a) Instagram and messenger-based sellers with 20–300 DMs a day (clothing, cosmetics, handmade, food) — core. (b) Small online shops with a Divar, Torob or own-site presence that also take orders by DM. (c) Clinics, salons and course sellers that sell by appointment through DM. Not targeted at first: large brands (they build in-house) and sellers under about 10 DMs a day (the saving is too small). |
| Value proposition | Replies in Persian within seconds, 24 hours a day: price, stock, size, shipping and payment-link answers, with hand-off to the owner for anything it is unsure about. Pro plan (1,000 conversations a month) replaces about 30 hours of manual chatting a month \[D: 1,000 × 60% usage × 3 min, 3 min is an A\]; at the 1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance (about 143,000 toman an hour \[D\]) that is about 4.29M toman of labour against a 2.49M toman price. Reference point: Divar charges 49,000 toman per ad for its own assistant \[S, per research notes\]. |
| Channels | Instagram professional-account DM (Meta API access for Iranian developers is unverified, see section 6); Rubika, Bale and Eitaa bots (domestic, reachable during whitelisted internet); website chat widget. Acquisition: Instagram ads and creators in the seller niche, seller Telegram/Instagram communities, referral credit (one free month per referral \[A\]), agency resellers. |
| Customer relationships | Self-serve onboarding in under 30 minutes (connect account, upload price list, test chat). One human customer-success person per 300 customers \[A\]. Weekly conversation report to the owner. Monthly plan billed in toman, indexed to the exchange rate (see risks). |
| Revenue streams | Monthly subscriptions: Starter 490,000 toman (200 conversations), Pro 2,490,000 (1,000), Business 14,900,000 (5,000) \[A, anchored to the labour saving above\]. Planned mix 65% / 31% / 4% \[A\] gives ARPU 1,686,400 toman a month (about $6.36) \[D\]. Free tier: 15 conversations for 3 months of trial \[A\]. |
| Key resources | Domestic GPU inference node (RTX 6000 Ada 48 GB, Sindad plan 150M toman a month \[S\]); an open-weight 8–9B model tuned on Persian sales dialogues; a Persian product-catalogue retrieval layer; 2 engineers and 1 customer-success hire. |
| Key activities | Model quality work in Persian (the largest risk); channel connectors; catalogue ingestion; seller onboarding; keeping messenger APIs and prices up to date. |
| Key partners | Domestic GPU/cloud host (Sindad or equivalent); payment gateway (Zarinpal and similar, worst-case 1% fee \[S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%\]); seller-community admins and agencies as resellers; bot platforms of Bale and Eitaa. |
| Cost structure | Fixed: team 159.9M toman a month, GPU node 150M, other infrastructure 10M, accounting 8M, marketing 15M = 342.9M toman a month at full run rate (about $1,293) \[D\]; one-time setup 150M \[A\]. Variable: gateway 1% of revenue; extra customer-success hire per 300 customers; extra GPU node whenever the load passes one node's capacity. |

sections_md.revenue:
Break-even is about 205 paying customers \[D: 342.9M ÷ (1,686,400 × 0.99)\] with one GPU node and no extra hire. The three scenarios below ramp customers linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure. Launch costs (150M setup) fall in month 1.

| Scenario | Paying customers at month 12 / 24 | Break-even month | Peak cash need (toman) | Month-24 MRR | Month-24 monthly profit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Conservative | 60 / 180 | not within 24 months | 5,009M (about $18,900) | 304M (about $1,144) | −42M |
| Base | 150 / 500 | 14 | 2,691M (about $10,100) | 843M (about $3,178) | +305M |
| Optimistic | 350 / 1,200 | 9 | 1,554M (about $5,900) | 2,024M (about $7,628) | +1,063M |

Customer counts are \[A\]. For scale, 500 customers would be a small share of the sellers I could find counts for, but those counts conflict (400K active stores vs 1.7M businesses, dates unclear), so the base case is a hypothesis to test with a paid pilot, not a market-sized forecast. In the base case cumulative cash is still −817M toman at month 24, so payback comes after month 24.
sections_md.sensitivities:
| Change | Break-even month | Peak cash need | Month-24 profit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| None | 14 | 2,691M | +305M |
| GPU price doubles | 17 | 4,722M | +5M |
| Prices 30% lower | 17 | 3,353M | +55M |
| Customers 50% lower (75 / 250) | 21 | 4,139M | +74M |

The model fixes the customer path, so churn does not change these rows; it only changes lifetime value. At 8% monthly churn \[A\], lifetime revenue per customer is about 20.9M toman \[D: 1,686,400 × 0.99 ÷ 0.08\]. Modelled acquisition cost is only marketing plus half a customer-success salary, about 0.6–1.9M toman per new customer \[D\], which leaves out founder sales time, so treat the LTV-to-CAC ratio as an upper bound and measure real CAC in the pilot.
sections_md.risks:
- Rial drift: the dollar rate rose 14.7% in the first 17 days of October and 30.6% since August \[D\]. Toman prices need monthly indexing; the GPU cost moves with it, but salaries and ad costs may lag or lead.
- Persian quality of an 8–9B model may be too weak for selling; a larger model would need about 2–4 times the GPU cost \[A\], close to the “GPU price doubles” row.
- Whitelisted internet and shutdowns: customers on Instagram lose service during shutdowns, which hits usage-based value.
- Competitors (Novin Hub, Artin Bot and similar) exist; their prices were not verified.
sections_md.unverified:
- Competitor subscription prices for Instagram DM bots in Iran.
- Whether Iranian developers can obtain Meta's Advanced Access and Business Verification for the Instagram messaging API; if not, the Instagram channel needs a different route and the segment shrinks.
- Bale and Eitaa bot API terms and fees.
- The current price of a plain CPU server (not needed for the GPU-based costs above).
- Zarinpal's exact fee (sources say 0.05%, 0.5% and 1%; the model uses 1%) and VAT (10% or 12%; the plan prices are shown before VAT).
- Real tokens per conversation and Persian throughput: both need a one-week benchmark on the actual node before any commitment.

Check run: all \[D\] figures above were recomputed by running the cost and revenue model in code on 22 Oct 2026.

2.title: Product title, description and SEO writer for Digikala, Basalam and Torob listings
2.verdict_md: Verdict: GPU cost is negligible (about 154 toman per listing), so the business is decided by fixed cost and by whether sellers will pay when free chatbots exist. It breaks even at about 194 paying customers; in the base case that is month 15, with peak cash need of about 2.8 billion toman (about $10,700). The market size and competitor prices could not be verified (section 6), so the customer counts are hypotheses. Tags: \[S\] sourced, \[D\] derived and recomputed by code, \[A\] assumption.

sections_md.canvas:
| Block | Content |
| --- | --- |
| Customer segments | (a) Marketplace sellers with 50–2,000 SKUs who list products themselves on Digikala, Basalam or Torob-linked shops — core. (b) Importers and wholesalers adding new catalogue lines every month. (c) Small agencies and freelancers who write listings for several shops (resellers). Not targeted: the largest brands (own content teams) and sellers with under about 20 listings (too little volume to pay a subscription). |
| Value proposition | Turns a product name, attributes and a photo into a Persian title, description, bullet features, keywords and meta text in the format each marketplace expects, in seconds, in bulk from a spreadsheet. Writing one listing by hand at 20 minutes \[A\] costs about 47,700 toman of labour at the 1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance (143,023 toman an hour \[D\]); our price is 3,950–5,900 toman per listing, 8–12% of that \[D\]. |
| Channels | Web app with CSV/Excel upload and copy-out per marketplace; WooCommerce and similar plugin; marketplace seller communities and Instagram/Telegram groups; SEO content on Persian search terms; agency partnerships. Direct publishing into Digikala or Basalam panels depends on their APIs and is not assumed. |
| Customer relationships | Self-serve with a brand-voice and category-template setup; one customer-success person per 300 customers \[A\]; quality guarantee (free regeneration, human-edited samples for the first batch); monthly credits that roll over for one month \[A\]. |
| Revenue streams | Monthly credit packs: Starter 590,000 toman (100 listings), Growth 2,490,000 (500), Pro 7,900,000 (2,000) \[A, anchored to the labour cost above\]. Mix 60% / 32% / 8% \[A\] gives ARPU 1,782,800 toman a month (about $6.72) \[D\]. Free trial: 5 listings. |
| Key resources | Persian-tuned 8–9B model on a domestic GPU node (Sindad plan, 150M toman a month \[S\]); per-category templates and SEO keyword data; 2 engineers and 1 customer-success/editor hire. |
| Key activities | Persian quality and factual-accuracy checks (no invented specifications); marketplace format rules and category templates; bulk-processing pipeline; seller onboarding and content marketing. |
| Key partners | Domestic GPU/cloud host; payment gateway (Zarinpal and similar, 1% worst case \[S, sources conflict\]); seller-community admins, agencies and plugin marketplaces as resellers. |
| Cost structure | Same fixed base as service #1: team 159.9M toman a month, GPU node 150M, other infrastructure 10M, accounting 8M, marketing 15M = 342.9M a month (about $1,293) \[D\]; one-time setup 150M \[A\]. Variable: 1% gateway fee and an extra customer-success hire per 300 customers. |

- Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct \[D\]).
- Low price per listing (8–12% of the labour cost) leaves room to raise prices if quality is proven.

- Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.

3.title: Product photo cleaner and studio-background generator
3.verdict_md: Verdict: GPU cost is small (about 598 toman per image, gross margin 87–91%), but the business is fixed-cost heavy and breaks even at about 229 paying customers. In the base case that is month 17, with peak cash need of about 3,381M toman (about $12,700) and +227M toman a month at month 24; the conservative case does not break even within 24 months. Two points change the plan: the popular BRIA RMBG-2.0 cut-out model is licensed non-commercial \[S\], so the model must be BiRefNet (MIT) or a licensed alternative; and the generative studio-background step must keep the product's shape and label unchanged, which small open image models do not guarantee, so a human check is part of the plan. No Iranian seller count or Iranian competitor price could be verified, so all customer counts are hypotheses \[A\]. Tags: \[S\] sourced, \[D\] derived and recomputed by code, \[A\] assumption.

sections_md.risks:
- Licence: BRIA RMBG-2.0 is CC BY-NC 4.0, so commercial use needs a commercial agreement with BRIA \[S, Hugging Face model page\]; BiRefNet is MIT \[S\] and is the planned model. The licence of whichever generative background model is used must be read before launch.
- Product fidelity: a generated background that alters the product, colour or logo causes returns and disputes; this needs human sampling and may add editor headcount.
- Free and foreign substitutes: phone-based editors and VPN-accessible tools (remove.bg, Canva-type tools) are available to sellers with a VPN; the case rests on bulk processing, marketplace sizes, Persian support and toman payment.
- Marketplace-built tools: Digikala or Basalam could add photo clean-up to their seller panels; I found no evidence either way.
- Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 \[D\]); the GPU plan is rial-priced.
- Throughput is an assumption: a real benchmark of the chosen pipeline on the rented node could move the GPU cost per image by a factor of two or more, which the GPU-doubles row covers.

4.title: CRM follow-up agent (drafts follow-ups, schedules calls, scores leads)
4.verdict_md: Verdict: the unit economics are strong (GPU about 54,400 toman per seat-month, gross margin 91–92%), but this is a B2B product with a sales hire and a larger team, so fixed cost is 457.5M toman a month and break-even needs about 75 paying companies. The base case (30 companies at month 12, 100 at month 24) breaks even only in month 21, with peak cash need of about 5,427M toman (about $20,500) and +112M toman a month at month 24; the conservative case never breaks even and a doubled GPU price, 30% lower prices or 50% fewer customers each push break-even past month 24. The market is contested by established Iranian CRMs that are adding AI themselves (Didar, per search-result headlines), and no CRM price list or seat count could be verified, so customer counts are hypotheses \[A\]. Lead scoring on a small company's own data is weak statistically; the realistic product is follow-up drafting and reminders, which small open Persian models can do at acceptable quality only after testing. Tags: \[S\] sourced, \[D\] derived and recomputed by code, \[A\] assumption.

5.title: Persian ad copy and campaign generator for SMS, Telegram and native ads
5.verdict_md: Verdict: GPU cost is negligible (about 136 toman per copy pack, gross margin 97%), so the result is decided by fixed cost and by how many agencies and shops will pay a subscription for something free chatbots also do. It breaks even at about 174 paying customers; in the base case that is month 16, with peak cash need of about 3,110M toman (about $11,700) and +308M toman a month at month 24. The conservative case does not break even in 24 months, and with 50% fewer customers the base case only just reaches break-even at month 24. The market size, SMS and ad-placement rules for Iran, and competitor prices could not be verified (section 6), so customer counts are hypotheses \[A\]. Telegram is a filtered platform in Iran and its ad market depends on VPN use, which I did not size. Tags: \[S\] sourced, \[D\] derived and recomputed by code, \[A\] assumption.

6.title: Competitor price monitor with repricing suggestions
6.verdict_md: Verdict: this is mostly a data-collection product, not a GPU product: the variable cost is scraping servers (about 214 toman per SKU-month, gross margin 90–96%), and buying the data from a third-party scraper instead would cost about 66,850 toman per SKU-month \[D\] and destroy the margin, so the company must run its own collectors. It breaks even at about 211 paying sellers; in the base case that is month 17, with peak cash need of about 2,292M toman (about $8,600) and +127M toman a month at month 24, a thin margin. The conservative case and the 50%-fewer-customers case never break even, and a 30% price cut leaves break-even at month 24 with +5M profit. The service depends on marketplaces tolerating automated price collection, which I could not confirm (the Torob scraper listing says Torob's search API only answers from inside Iran \[S\]); the AI part (matching products across shops, explaining suggestions) is a small share of the work. Customer counts are hypotheses \[A\]. Tags: \[S\] sourced, \[D\] derived and recomputed by code, \[A\] assumption.

Not targeted: sellers with under about 50 SKUs and brands that set one fixed price. |

7.title: Inflation-aware price list (reprices catalogs from the exchange rate and cost index)
7.verdict_md: Verdict: this is mostly a rules engine, not a GPU product, so variable cost is tiny (about 57 toman per SKU-month, gross margin 93–97%) and the case turns on fixed cost: break-even at about 122 paying customers. In the base case that is month 14, with peak cash need of about 1,821M toman (about $6,900) and +261M toman a month at month 24, and even the 30%-lower-price and 50%-fewer-customer cases break even by month 17 and 21. The per-server capacity (300,000 SKU-months) is my assumption, not a benchmark, and the exchange-rate and cost-index data feed, its licence and its price could not be verified; the figures also depend on Iranian inflation staying high, since value falls if the rial stabilises. The "AI" part is limited to reading messy supplier price lists, which small open models may do poorly in Persian without testing. Customer counts are hypotheses \[A\]. 8.title: Customer review summarizer and sentiment dashboard
8.verdict_md: Verdict: not convincing as modelled. GPU cost is about 19 toman per review and gross margin is 76–87%, but the review volumes a paying store or brand has are low, so revenue per customer is about 1.96M toman a month against 342.9M toman of fixed cost. Break-even needs about 177 paying customers; the base case (60 at month 12, 200 at month 24) reaches it only in month 23, with peak cash need of about 4,343M toman (about $16,400) and +44M toman a month at month 24, cumulative cash still −4,277M \[D\]. The conservative case never breaks even and all three stress cases (GPU price doubled, prices 30% lower, customers halved) stay loss-making through month 24. The classification part is cheap and proven: a Persian BERT sentiment model reaches F1 92.42 on binary SentiPers digital-product opinions \[S\], so a dedicated 150M-toman GPU node is arguably the wrong design for this service and a CPU or shared-GPU design would change the result; I did not model it. The Digikala and Snappfood sentiment dataset's licence is listed as unknown \[S\], which matters for training. Customer counts are hypotheses \[A\]. Tags: \[S\] sourced, \[D\] derived and recomputed by code, \[A\] assumption.

9.title: Store builder from photos or voice notes
9.verdict_md: Verdict: marginal. GPU cost is only about 250 toman per product listing (vision draft plus optional speech-to-text) and gross margin is 94–97%, but a micro-seller can only pay a small amount, so revenue per customer is about 353,100 toman a month against 352.9M toman of fixed cost. Break-even needs about 1,014 paying customers (about 1,440 when customer-success hires are added in whole steps). The base case (500 at month 12, 1,800 at month 24) reaches it in month 21, with a peak cash need of about 4,189M toman (about $15,790) and only +52M toman a month at month 24; cumulative cash is still −4,059M. The conservative case never breaks even and all three stress cases (GPU price doubled, prices 30% lower, customers halved) stay loss-making through month 24. The service also competes with established store builders that already bundle hosting, payment and shipping, and I found no sourced count of micro-sellers who would pay. Persian speech recognition on noisy voice notes is weaker than the leaderboard figures suggest (see section 5). Customer counts are hypotheses \[A\]. Tags: \[S\] sourced, \[D\] derived and recomputed by code, \[A\] assumption.

10.title: Personalized SMS and push campaign engine
10.verdict_md: Verdict: weak as modelled. If an LLM writes every message, GPU cost is about 23 toman per message, and because a campaign customer sends tens of thousands of messages a month (90,000 on average at the plan mix below \[D\]), GPU cost eats most of the margin: gross margin is 65% on Starter but 31% on Growth and 7.5% on Scale. Revenue per customer is about 2.78M toman a month. The base case (80 customers at month 12, 300 at month 24) never breaks even within 24 months: peak cash need is about 4,900M toman (about $18,500), month-24 profit is −169M toman a month and five GPU nodes are needed. Only the optimistic case (200 / 750) breaks even, in month 17, with +133M toman a month at month 24 and cumulative cash still −2,558M. All three stress cases stay loss-making. A design that fills templates per segment instead of calling the model per recipient would cost far less GPU time, but I did not model it. The carrier SMS fee is excluded because I could not verify any Iranian SMS price (see section 6), so the customer is assumed to buy SMS credit from its own panel. Customer counts are hypotheses \[A\]. Tags: \[S\] sourced, \[D\] derived and recomputed by code, \[A\] assumption.

11.title: Website and app chatbot trained on the company's own documents
11.verdict_md: Verdict: viable if the customer counts are reached, and the numbers are not fragile to cost. GPU cost is about 599 toman per conversation and gross margin is 74–81%. Revenue per customer is about 2.19M toman a month against 347.9M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 161 paying customers. The base case (120 at month 12, 450 at month 24) breaks even in month 14, with a peak cash need of about 2,675M toman (about $10,100) and +439M toman a month at month 24; cumulative cash is nearly back to zero (−184M) at month 24. The conservative case (40 / 150) does not break even within 24 months but is close (−23M a month at month 24). Doubling the GPU price, cutting prices 30% or halving customers each delay break-even to months 16–20 and leave month-24 profit positive. The weak point is the customer count: 450 paying business customers in two years is a hypothesis with no sourced market size behind it. It also depends on an 8–9B open-weight model answering in Persian from retrieved passages without inventing facts, which I could not test. Customer counts are hypotheses \[A\]. Tags: \[S\] sourced, \[D\] derived and recomputed by code, \[A\] assumption.

12.title: Persian voice bot that replaces call-center menus
12.verdict_md: Verdict: marginal, and dependent on a licence I could not confirm. GPU cost is about 813 toman per call minute (speech-to-text, language model and speech synthesis together, 4.2 GPU-seconds per minute \[D\]) and gross margin is 33–52%, because the price a call center will pay is capped by the cost of a human agent-minute, which at the 1405 minimum wage is only 2,384 toman. Revenue per customer is about 67.9M toman a month against 461.7M toman of fixed cost. The base case (8 customers at month 12, 25 at month 24) breaks even in month 19, with a peak cash need of about 4,171M toman (about $15,700) and +220M toman a month at month 24; cumulative cash is still −3,579M. The conservative case (3 / 10) never breaks even, and doubling the GPU price, cutting prices 30% or halving customers each leave the base case loss-making through month 24. The two open Persian speech-synthesis model families I opened are licensed non-commercial, so a commercial voice must be licensed or trained, which I priced only as an assumption. Customer counts are hypotheses \[A\]. Tags: \[S\] sourced, \[D\] derived and recomputed by code, \[A\] assumption.

13.title: Call transcription and quality scoring
13.verdict_md: Verdict: viable on the numbers, with weak evidence on demand and accuracy. GPU cost is about 17,800 toman per audio hour (batch speech-to-text, speaker separation and a scoring pass, 154 GPU-seconds an hour \[D\]) and gross margin is 58–71%. Revenue per customer is about 45.4M toman a month, so the 352.9M toman fixed cost is covered by about 8 customers. The base case (20 customers at month 12, 70 at month 24) breaks even in month 7, with a peak cash need of about 1,328M toman (about $5,000) and +1,631M toman a month at month 24. Even the conservative case (8 / 25) breaks even in month 12, and doubling the GPU price, cutting prices 30% or halving customers each still break even by month 15. The weak points are the customer counts (no sourced count of Iranian call centers that record and would pay), and Persian accuracy on phone audio: the best open Persian model I found scores 21.97 word error rate on a customer-service set, and quality scores built on transcripts that wrong are noisy. Customer counts are hypotheses \[A\]. Tags: \[S\] sourced, \[D\] derived and recomputed by code, \[A\] assumption.

14.title: Helpdesk ticket triage and draft replies
14.verdict_md: Verdict: viable on the numbers, with demand unverified. GPU cost is only about 86 toman per ticket and gross margin is 96–97%, so the business is carried by fixed cost, not model cost. Revenue per customer is about 22.0M toman a month against 347.9M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 16 paying customers. The base case (20 customers at month 12, 80 at month 24) breaks even in month 11, with a peak cash need of about 1,892M toman (about $7,100) and +1,323M toman a month at month 24. The conservative case (8 / 30) breaks even in month 17, and doubling the GPU price, cutting prices 30% or halving customers each still break even by month 15. The weak points are the market and the quality of Persian drafts: I found no sourced count of Iranian software firms, ISPs and online businesses with a ticketing helpdesk of 5 or more agents, and 80 such customers in two years is a hypothesis. Customer counts are hypotheses \[A\]. Tags: \[S\] sourced, \[D\] derived and recomputed by code, \[A\] assumption.

15.title: Meeting recorder with Persian minutes and action items
15.verdict_md: Verdict: viable in the base case, but the margin depends on speech-recognition cost, which I could not measure. GPU cost is about 17,800 toman per meeting hour (144 of 154 GPU-seconds are speech recognition and speaker separation \[D\], on a throughput assumption \[A\]) and gross margin is 52–61%, so unlike a text-only service one GPU node serves only about 26 customers \[D\]. Revenue per customer is about 13.5M toman a month against 347.9M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 27 customers on paper and 42 once the second GPU node is counted \[D\]. The base case (30 customers at month 12, 120 at month 24) breaks even in month 14, with a peak cash need of about 2,373M toman (about $8,900) and +468M toman a month at month 24. The conservative case (10 / 40) does not break even within 24 months (about −14M a month at month 24), and doubling the GPU price also prevents break-even; halving customers delays it to month 19. The weak points are Persian accuracy on multi-speaker room audio (the best open Persian model I found scores 11–22 word error rate on four test sets, none of them meetings, and the widely used whisper-large-v3 scores 36–76 on the same sets \[S\]), the 30x throughput assumption, and the customer counts, which have no sourced market size behind them. Customer counts are hypotheses \[A\]. Tags: \[S\] sourced, \[D\] derived and recomputed by code, \[A\] assumption.

16.title: Formal letter and administrative correspondence drafter
16.verdict_md: Verdict: marginal. Model cost is negligible (about 118 toman per letter, gross margin 97–98% \[D\]), but each customer pays only about 9.35M toman a month against 347.9M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 38 paying organisations on paper and 42 once the customer-success hires are counted \[D\]. The base case (30 customers at month 12, 120 at month 24) breaks even in month 14, with a peak cash need of about 2,631M toman (about $9,900) and +615M toman a month at month 24. The conservative case (10 / 40) does not break even within 24 months (−15M a month at month 24; cumulative cash −4,925M). Doubling the GPU price, cutting prices 30% or halving customers delay break-even to months 17–20 and leave month-24 profit positive. The weak points are willingness to pay and the customer count: letters can also be drafted with general chat assistants, I found no Iranian price for a dedicated product, and a domestic letter-writing app already exists (found only as a search-result title, so its price is unknown). No sourced count of Iranian offices or contractors that would pay exists in this model. Quality of formal Persian register in an 8–9B open model is untested. Customer counts are hypotheses \[A\]. Tags: \[S\] sourced, \[D\] derived and recomputed by code, \[A\] assumption.

No count of office staff who write formal letters, or of contractors, was found.

The user states the purpose, recipient and key facts; the service drafts the letter in the correct formal Persian register, with salutation, reference line, subject line and closing formulas, and adjusts tone for a ministry, a bank or a client. It also rewrites received letters into a summary and a reply draft. A domestic app for writing letters and administrative texts exists on Cafe Bazaar [S, search-result title only; the page is blocked to fetch, so features and price are not verified].

Direct sales to office managers and company owners; Telegram and Instagram groups of contractors and administrative staff; Cafe Bazaar and web app listing; bundling with accounting or office-software vendors.

Free trial of 30 letters [A]; a library of the customer's own letter templates and letterhead; one customer-success person per 30 customers [A]. Monthly plan billed in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

17.title: Persian speech-to-text API
17.verdict_md: Verdict: viable on the numbers, with price competition and the model licence as the open questions. GPU cost is about 231 toman per audio minute (2 GPU-seconds a minute on a 30x throughput assumption \[A\]; about $0.052 an audio hour \[D\]) and gross margin is 84–87%. Revenue per customer is about 30.8M toman a month against 347.9M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 12 paying customers \[D\]. The base case (20 customers at month 12, 80 at month 24) breaks even in month 9, with a peak cash need of about 1,537M toman (about $5,800) and +1,716M toman a month at month 24. Even the conservative case (8 / 30) breaks even in month 14, and doubling the GPU price, cutting prices 30% or halving customers each still break even by month 13. The weak points are price and licence: foreign speech APIs list far lower prices than the plans below (Soniox $0.12 an audio hour, Google batch $0.003 a minute \[S\]) and are hard to pay for from Iran \[A\], developers can also self-host open Persian models, and I could not confirm that the best open Persian recognition model (gooya-v1.4, 11–22 word error rate on four sets \[S\]) may be used commercially. The customer counts have no sourced count of Iranian developers behind them. Customer counts are hypotheses \[A\]. Tags: \[S\] sourced, \[D\] derived and recomputed by code, \[A\] assumption.

18.title: Persian text-to-speech with custom brand voices
18.verdict_md: Verdict: viable on the numbers, but blocked until a commercially usable Persian voice model exists. GPU cost is only about 257 toman per 1,000 characters (2.2 GPU-seconds on a 30x throughput assumption \[A\]) and gross margin is 95–96%, so the business is carried by fixed cost of 412.1M toman a month, which about 10 paying customers cover at 42.8M toman each \[D\]. The base case (20 customers at month 12, 80 at month 24) breaks even in month 8, with a peak cash need of about 1,733M toman (about $6,500) and +2,904M toman a month at month 24. The conservative case (8 / 30) breaks even in month 13, and doubling the GPU price, cutting prices 30% or halving customers each still break even by month 12. The weak points are the licence and the demand. The open Persian voice models I found are non-commercial (a Persian MMS voice is CC BY-NC 4.0, and a Persian XTTS voice is under the Coqui licence that restricts commercial use while its metadata says MIT \[S\]), so a sellable service needs a model trained on licensed voice data, which is not costed beyond the setup and royalty lines below. Custom voices also need documented consent from the speaker. There is no sourced count of Iranian buyers of synthetic speech. Customer counts are hypotheses \[A\]. Tags: \[S\] sourced, \[D\] derived and recomputed by code, \[A\] assumption.

19.title: No-code AI bot builder for Bale, Eitaa and Telegram
19.verdict_md: Verdict: marginal. GPU cost is about 272 toman per conversation and gross margin is 76–85%, but a small business pays only about 4.5M toman a month on average against 357.9M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 80 paying customers on paper and 97 once the customer-success hires are counted \[D\]. The base case (80 customers at month 12, 400 at month 24) breaks even in month 13, with a peak cash need of about 2,460M toman (about $9,300) and +769M toman a month at month 24. The conservative case (30 / 120) breaks even only in month 21 with a peak cash need of about 4,267M toman and cumulative cash still −4,078M at month 24. Doubling the GPU price, cutting prices 30% or halving customers delay break-even to months 15–18. The weak points are churn (micro-sellers cancel often; 6% a month is assumed), the dependence on three messengers whose bot rules and reachability I could not verify (Bale publishes four bot libraries and reports over 30,000 active bots \[S\], but I found no bot interface documentation for Eitaa and Telegram is filtered in Iran \[A\]), and the absence of any found Iranian bot-builder price. Customer counts are hypotheses \[A\]. Tags: \[S\] sourced, \[D\] derived and recomputed by code, \[A\] assumption.

- Platform dependence: each messenger controls its bot interface, rate limits and rules; I could not verify Eitaa's or Telegram's current bot terms, and a rule change can remove a channel.
- Reachability: Telegram is filtered in Iran \[A\] and Iran had a near-total internet blackout from 18 June 2025 \[S, techradar.com\]; bots on domestic messengers keep working only if the platform and hosting stay reachable.
- Churn and low ARPU: with about 4.5M toman a month per customer, small price or churn changes move break-even by many months (prices −30% adds 5 months).
- Free alternatives: sellers can use free bot templates and general chat assistants; I found no Iranian bot-builder price to compare.
- Accuracy: wrong prices or stock in a sales bot cost the seller money; the model's behaviour on Persian catalogs is untested.

20.title: Chat translator for Persian, Arabic, Turkish and English trade
20.verdict_md: Verdict: weak on these assumptions. Model cost is negligible (about 68 toman per message, gross margin 87–92% \[D\]), but revenue per customer is only about 3.0M toman a month against 396M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 132 paying customers on paper and 182 once the customer-success hires are counted \[D\]. The base case (60 customers at month 12, 300 at month 24) breaks even only in month 19, with a peak cash need of about 4,465M toman (about $16,800) and +243M toman a month at month 24; cumulative cash is still −3,684M at month 24, so the base case does not pay back within the horizon. The conservative case (25 / 100) never breaks even (−171M a month at month 24), and cutting prices 30% or halving customers also prevents break-even. Doubling the GPU price delays it to month 22. The weak points are the substitute and the translation quality: Google lists NMT translation at $20 per million characters with 500,000 characters free each month \[S\], free consumer translators exist \[A\], and I could not confirm that an 8–9B open model translates Persian, Iraqi Arabic and Turkish trade language well enough to be paid for. The customer counts have no sourced count of Iranian exporters behind them. Customer counts are hypotheses \[A\]. Tags: \[S\] sourced, \[D\] derived and recomputed by code, \[A\] assumption.

sections_md.risks:
- Free substitutes: general translators and chat assistants already translate between these languages at no or low cost; a paid tool must win on trade glossaries and chat integration, so the price per message may have to be lower still.

21.title: Invoice and receipt OCR to accounting entries (Persian digits, Jalali dates)
21.verdict_md: Verdict: weak on these assumptions. Model cost is small (about 290 toman per document including staff re-checks, gross margin 84–90% \[D\]), but the plans below charge only 1,167–1,933 toman per document, so revenue per customer is about 1.32M toman a month against 396M toman of fixed cost; break-even needs about 309 paying customers on paper and 568 once the customer-success hires are counted \[D\]. The base case (100 customers at month 12, 450 at month 24) never breaks even within 24 months: it is still losing 77M toman a month at month 24 and its cumulative cash is −6,301M toman (about $23,800), so the peak cash need is a floor, not a peak. The conservative case (40 / 150) loses 277M a month at month 24; only the optimistic case (250 / 1,200) breaks even, in month 17, with +255M a month at month 24. Doubling the GPU price, cutting prices 30% or halving customers each leaves the base case unprofitable. The service also depends on an unproven capability: I found no accuracy figure for any open vision model on Persian invoices (Persian digits, Jalali dates, tax IDs), and the only Persian invoice sample set I found is 50 synthetic images. The customer counts have no sourced count of Iranian shops or bookkeeping offices behind them. Customer counts are hypotheses \[A\]. Tags: \[S\] sourced, \[D\] derived and recomputed by code, \[A\] assumption.

Pool: the Iranian Institute of Certified Accountants says it has more than 6,000 members \[S, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iranian\_Institute\_of\_Certified\_Accountants, read 24 Oct 2026; no date given\], which counts certified accountants only, not the many uncertified bookkeepers and shop owners; a search headline (eghtesadnews, undated) reports 12 million tax-registered payers \[S, headline only, page not opened\]. System Group, maker of the Hamkaran accounting software, says it has served over 53,000 clients since 1987, a group-wide figure \[S, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/System\_Group, read 24 Oct 2026\]. 22.title: E-invoicing and tax filing assistant for the national tax system
22.verdict_md: Verdict: weak on these assumptions. Model cost is almost nil (about 25 toman per invoice, gross margin 98% \[D\]) because only an assumed 20% of invoices need a language-model check and the rest are rule-checked \[A\], but revenue per customer is only about 0.80M toman a month against 396M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 498 paying customers on paper and 1,103 once the customer-success hires are counted \[D\]. The base case (150 customers at month 12, 700 at month 24) never breaks even within 24 months: it still loses 135M toman a month at month 24 and its cumulative cash is −6,864M toman (about $25,900), so the peak cash need is a floor. The conservative case (60 / 250) loses 308M a month at month 24; only the optimistic case (400 / 2,000) breaks even, in month 18, and its cumulative cash is still −3,231M at month 24. Doubling the GPU price, cutting prices 30% or halving customers each leaves the base case unprofitable. The commercial problem is the substitute: accounting packages already advertise sending invoices to the tax system (search headline only), the portal itself is the government's, and an open-source library for the same API exists \[S\], so the assistant has to sell on error explanations and return drafting, not on submission. The GPU node (150M of the 396M fixed cost) is far larger than this workload needs, so a CPU-only version would change the result; I kept the node so the data stays on a domestic GPU host like the other services. The customer counts have no sourced count of Iranian businesses behind them. Customer counts are hypotheses \[A\]. Tags: \[S\] sourced, \[D\] derived and recomputed by code, \[A\] assumption.

A guided assistant that checks each invoice against the tax system's field rules before it is sent, explains rejection messages in Persian, prepares the corrections and returns the tax system accepts, and drafts the periodic VAT return from the month's invoices for the owner or accountant to review and submit (the assistant never files on its own). Web app and Bale/Eitaa bot; plug-ins for popular accounting and shop software (not verified); accountants' associations and training courses; chambers of guilds; referral by bookkeeping offices.

23.title: Chat-based bookkeeping copilot
23.verdict_md: Verdict: weak on these assumptions. Model cost is small (about 77 toman per entry, gross margin 91–94% \[D\]), but revenue per customer is only about 0.345M toman a month ($1.30) against 394.8M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 1,156 paying customers on paper and 1,913 once customer-success hires are counted \[D\]. The base case (250 customers at month 12, 1,200 at month 24) never breaks even within 24 months: it loses 133M toman a month at month 24 and its cumulative cash is −6,798M toman (about $25,600), so that figure is a floor, not a peak. The conservative case (80 / 350) loses 312M a month at month 24; only the optimistic case (700 / 3,500) breaks even, in month 18, with a peak cash need of 4,120M toman and −3,030M cumulative at month 24. Doubling the GPU price, cutting prices 30% or halving customers each deepens the base loss. I set one customer-success person per 250 customers because at 100 per person (my first guess) support cost per customer exceeded revenue per customer and the base case lost 428M a month at month 24 \[D\]; that is the most sensitive assumption here. No Iranian bookkeeping-app price was found, so the price points are not anchored to a competitor; the only anchor is the labour of typing entries by hand. Whether an 8–9B model reliably reads Persian shorthand messages (amounts, Persian digits, informal words) was not tested. Customer counts are hypotheses \[A\], although the pool of self-employed people is large \[S, D\]. Tags: \[S\] sourced, \[D\] derived and recomputed by code, \[A\] assumption.

sections_md.risks:
- Willingness to pay: micro-businesses may expect a free chatbot; a low price per customer needs very low support cost, so the ratio of customers per support person decides the result.
- Free substitutes: general chatbots and spreadsheets already do part of this at no charge; I found no Iranian bookkeeping-app price to compare against.
- Habit and retention: the product works only if the owner records daily; churn above 6% would shorten customer life further.
- Accuracy and trust: a wrong amount or a mis-read Persian digit breaks trust in a financial record; an 8–9B model needs a confirmation step per entry.
- Data: ledgers are sensitive financial data; domestic hosting is assumed, and platform bot terms were not read.
- Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 \[D\]).

24.title: Bank statement categorizer and cash-flow forecast
24.verdict_md: Verdict: weak on these assumptions. Model cost is tiny (about 11 toman per statement line, gross margin 96.5–97.5% \[D\]) because categorising short lines is cheap and the forecast runs on a CPU, but revenue per customer is about 0.83M toman a month ($3.13) against 401.0M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 488 paying customers on paper and 1,027 once customer-success hires are counted \[D\]. The base case (120 customers at month 12, 500 at month 24) never breaks even within 24 months: it loses 212M toman a month at month 24 and its cumulative cash is −7,391M toman (about $27,900), so that figure is a floor. The conservative case (40 / 160) loses 343M a month at month 24; only the optimistic case (300 / 1,400) breaks even, in month 20, with a peak cash need of 4,837M toman. Doubling the GPU price, cutting prices 30% or halving customers each deepens the base loss. The structural problem is intake: I found no evidence that Iranian banks give third parties account-data APIs (a directory lists 37 Iranian institutions and marks none as having API access \[S\]), so customers would have to upload exported statements or screenshots, which adds friction and file-parsing work that was not costed. No Iranian competitor price was found. Customer counts are hypotheses \[A\] with no sourced count of eligible SMEs behind them. Tags: \[S\] sourced, \[D\] derived and recomputed by code, \[A\] assumption.

(b) Bookkeeping offices that process statements for many clients. (c) Online sellers who reconcile payment-gateway settlements against bank credits. Categorising one statement line by hand in a spreadsheet takes about 30 seconds \[A\], about 1,192 toman of labour at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance \[D\]); the plans below charge 350–600 toman per line, 29–50% of that \[D\], so the case rests on the forecast and the time saved on review, not on the typing alone. Forecasting is simple time-series work on a CPU; the model only reads the free-text descriptions. |
| Channels | Web app and Bale/Eitaa bot for uploads; bookkeeping offices and accountants' associations; guild chambers; content for owners about cash management. |

25.title: Cheque tracker with bounce-risk alerts
25.verdict_md: Verdict: weak on these assumptions. Model cost is small (about 83 toman per cheque entered, gross margin 97–98% \[D\]), but revenue per customer is about 0.875M toman a month ($3.30) against 407.1M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 470 paying customers on paper and 1,493 once customer-success hires are counted \[D\]. None of the three scenarios breaks even within 24 months: the base case (120 customers at month 12, 450 at month 24) loses 276M toman a month at month 24 and its cumulative cash is −8,099M toman (about $30,500), the conservative case (40 / 150) −8,819M, and even the optimistic case (300 / 1,200) still loses 106M a month with −6,446M cumulative; these cash figures are floors because losses continue. The price is also hard to justify per unit: the Small plan charges more per cheque than the assumed 3 minutes of manual logging costs, so the product has to sell on avoided losses, not on time saved \[D\]. The market need is real (the value of bounced cheques reached about 1,000 trillion rials in July 2024 \[S\]), but the central bank's cheque-inquiry data may not be available to a third party, and I did not find a way to get a payer's cheque history legally. Customer counts are hypotheses \[A\]. Tags: \[S\] sourced, \[D\] derived and recomputed by code, \[A\] assumption.

Pool: the value of bounced cheques hit about 1,000 trillion rials in July 2024, about $1.7 billion at the open-market rate, with more than 30% of returned cheques by volume in Tehran \[S, iranintl.com/en/202408241294, published 25 Aug 2024\]. sections_md.risks:
- Data access: a useful bounce-risk score needs the payer's cheque record from the central bank's system; whether a third party can query it, at what fee, and with whose consent was not found, and without it the score rests only on the user's own logs.
- Liability: a wrong "safe" flag on a payer who then bounces a cheque exposes the service to blame; flags must be framed as the user's own record, not a credit opinion.
- Pricing power: the Small plan is above the manual-logging cost per cheque, so willingness to pay depends on avoided losses and cannot be sourced from a competitor price.
- Rule changes: cheque law and the central bank's systems have changed repeatedly; I could not read the current rules.
- Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 \[D\]).

26.title: SME credit scoring for B2B trade credit
26.verdict_md: Verdict: weak on these assumptions, and licence-dependent. Per-query cost is dominated by data, not the model: the model costs about 317 toman per query, but I assumed 6,000 toman of data purchase per query because no data price was found, giving a gross margin of 62–77% \[D\]. Revenue per customer is about 4.88M toman a month ($18.39) against 485.9M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 146 paying customers on paper and 190 with hires counted \[D\]. The base case (30 customers at month 12, 120 at month 24) never breaks even within 24 months: it loses 196M toman a month at month 24 and its cumulative cash is −8,548M toman (about $32,200), a floor; the conservative case (10 / 40) loses 389M a month at month 24, and only the optimistic case (80 / 350) breaks even, in month 17, with a peak cash need of 5,162M toman, +388M a month at month 24 and −3,646M cumulative. Doubling the GPU price, cutting prices 30% or halving customers each deepens the base loss. A 2023 law created two kinds of licensed credit-scoring company, one using government-held national data and one using non-government data, and a paper proposes capping their fees at operating cost plus 30% \[S\]; this service would need the second kind of licence, and I could not confirm the requirements, the cost or whether a start-up can get one. I first priced at 10,000–20,000 toman per query with a 20,000 toman data cost, which gave negative margins on the two larger plans \[D\]; the data price is therefore the main uncertainty. Customer counts are hypotheses \[A\]. Tags: \[S\] sourced, \[D\] derived and recomputed by code, \[A\] assumption.

27.title: Payment and order fraud detection API
27.verdict_md: Verdict: weak on these assumptions, and dependent on data I could not confirm. The model cost is almost nil (about 4.5 toman per scored transaction, gross margin 70–95% \[D\]) because scoring is a CPU model and only an assumed 5% of transactions get a written explanation \[A\]; the economics are set by fixed cost. Revenue per customer is about 1.89M toman a month ($7.12) against 484.8M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 259 paying customers on paper and 358 with GPU nodes and hires counted \[D\]. The base case (80 customers at month 12, 350 at month 24) never breaks even within 24 months but is almost level at the end (−14M toman a month at month 24, cumulative cash −7,125M toman, about $26,900, a floor); the conservative case (30 / 120) loses 334M a month at month 24; only the optimistic case (200 / 900) breaks even, in month 18, with a peak cash need of 4,631M toman and +346M a month at month 24. Doubling the GPU price, cutting prices 30% or halving customers each leaves the base case loss-making. The market is large (Iranian e-commerce was 2.5 billion transactions in the first half of the Iranian year starting March 2025 \[S\]), but a fraud model needs labelled chargeback or fraud history and card or device data from customers, and I found no evidence on what Iranian gateways or merchants can share or what rules apply. The plan mix is the largest input: the 5% of customers that are payment providers send 2 million transactions each in the model. Customer counts are hypotheses \[A\]. Tags: \[S\] sourced, \[D\] derived and recomputed by code, \[A\] assumption.

28.title: Stock-exchange disclosure summarizer for Persian filings (information only, not investment advice)
28.verdict_md: Verdict: viable on these assumptions, with a thin margin of safety and unverified demand. GPU cost is about 136 toman per summary or answer (an assumed 1,500 tokens on a text model) and gross margin is 88–92% \[D\]. Revenue per customer is about 304,000 toman a month ($1.15) against 417.1M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 1,386 paying customers on paper and 1,754 with GPU nodes and hires counted \[D\]. The base case (1,000 customers at month 12, 5,000 at month 24) breaks even in month 15 with a peak cash need of 3,548M toman (about $13,372) and +569M toman a month at month 24; cumulative cash only returns to +193M by month 24. The conservative case (300 / 1,500) never breaks even and is still losing 76M a month at month 24 (cumulative cash −6,502M, about $24,509, a floor); the optimistic case (3,000 / 15,000) breaks even in month 9 with a peak cash need of 1,837M. GPU price doubled, prices 30% lower and customers halved each push base break-even to month 17, 19 and 20 but stay profitable at month 24. Against that, I found no competitor price, no current count of active retail traders (the only sourced count is 9 million registered shareholders in 2016), and no text on whether summarising filings for investors needs a licence; the exchange also closed for nine days and fell sharply in June 2025, which hits customer numbers directly. Persian financial-text accuracy of a small model, especially on numbers in statements, was not tested. Customer counts are hypotheses \[A\]. Tags: \[S\] sourced, \[D\] derived and recomputed by code, \[A\] assumption.

sections_md.risks:
- Market activity: the exchange closed for nine days during the June 2025 strikes, reopened with 3% daily price limits, fell about 200,000 index points to 2,788,000 and saw about 9 trillion toman leave the market \[S, iranwire.com/en/economy/142839, 30 Jun 2025, read 25 Oct 2026\]. Paying demand follows trading activity, so a weak market lowers both customers and retention.
- Advice line: summarising a filing is information, but short summaries can read as recommendations. Whether the Securities and Exchange Organization requires a licence for investor-facing summaries or alerts was not found; a general overview of Iran's securities law did not address investment advisers \[S, generisonline.com, read 25 Oct 2026\].
- Accuracy and liability: a wrong figure or a missed qualification in an audit opinion can cost a user money; each summary needs numeric checks against the source and an easy correction path, which the analyst hire in the model only partly covers.
- Free and bundled substitutes: filings are public, and brokers and portfolio apps can add summaries as a feature; I could not read competitor pages to compare price or quality.
- Data access: automated collection from the exchange's disclosure portal may be restricted by its terms or rate limits; the terms were not checked.
- Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 \[D\]).

29.title: Contract and budget indexation calculator for inflation clauses
29.verdict_md: Verdict: marginal. Model cost is small (about 363 toman per calculation, gross margin 91–94% \[D\]) because the arithmetic is deterministic and the model only reads the clause and writes the explanation; the economics are set by fixed cost. Revenue per customer is about 323,450 toman a month ($1.22) against 412.1M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 1,287 paying customers on paper and 1,748 with hires counted \[D\]. The base case (500 customers at month 12, 2,500 at month 24) breaks even in month 20 with a peak cash need of 4,845M toman (about $18,264) and +167M a month at month 24, but cumulative cash is still −4,359M, so payback is well beyond month 24. The conservative case (150 / 700) never breaks even (−225M a month at month 24, cumulative cash −7,917M, about $29,844, a floor); the optimistic case (1,500 / 8,000) breaks even in month 13 with +1,262M a month at month 24. Doubling the GPU price delays base break-even to month 23 with +17M at month 24; cutting prices 30% or halving customers leaves the base case loss-making. Demand rests on very high inflation (73% year on year in April 2026 \[S\]) and on rules that cap rent increases and make price adjustment a main source of contractor disputes, but I found no count of landlords or contractors who would pay, no price of a competing tool, and no source for the official indices the calculator would read. Customer counts are hypotheses \[A\]. Tags: \[S\] sourced, \[D\] derived and recomputed by code, \[A\] assumption.

| Customer segments | (a) Small and mid-size contractors and subcontractors with price-adjustment (ta'dil) or inflation clauses in public and private contracts, who must prepare adjustment claims — core by revenue. The labour replaced is reading the clause, finding index values, calculating and writing the notice by hand: 20 minutes \[A\], about 47,674 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance \[D\]); the plans below charge 3,200–4,900 toman per calculation, 7–10% of that \[D\]. sections_md.risks:
- Free substitutes: rent-increase and indexation calculators are simple enough that free web calculators or an agent's spreadsheet may satisfy landlords; I could not read any competitor page to compare, so the landlord plan may not sell at all.
- Unsettled rules: the rent cap in force for 2026 and the way it is set (50%–100% of provincial inflation under the 2024 law \[S\]) were not confirmed, and the sources found conflict on the figures; a calculator that applies a wrong cap creates liability.
- Index data: the calculator needs official index values (price indices and construction cost indices) in machine-readable form; their publishers, licences and update lag were not confirmed.
- Contract variety: adjustment clauses differ by employer and contract template, and a study found no unified guideline for calculating adjustment damages \[S, qgl.lri.ir/article\_248464\_en.html\]; clause reading errors can change a claim by a large amount, so human review is needed for large contracts.
- Concentration and timing: lease renewals cluster in some months, and contractor claims depend on public-sector payment behaviour; revenue may be seasonal, which the straight-line customer path does not show.
- Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 \[D\]).

30.title: Payroll and social-insurance calculation assistant
30.verdict_md: Verdict: marginal. Model cost is small (about 109 toman per employee-month, gross margin 98% \[D\]) because the pay, insurance and tax arithmetic is deterministic code and the model only reads attendance notes and exceptions and writes flags; the economics are set by fixed cost. Revenue per customer is about 752,000 toman a month ($2.83) against 429.4M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 577 paying customers on paper and 825 with hires counted \[D\]. The base case (300 customers at month 12, 1,500 at month 24) breaks even in month 18 with a peak cash need of 4,595M toman (about $17,321) and +318M a month at month 24, but cumulative cash is still −3,340M, so payback is beyond month 24. Doubling the GPU price delays base break-even to month 21 and keeps month 24 profitable (+168M); cutting prices 30% or halving customers each leaves the base case loss-making through month 24. Correctness against the current insurance and tax rules is a hard requirement that I could not check line by line. Customer counts are hypotheses \[A\]. 31.title: Contract drafting and review in Persian
31.verdict_md: Verdict: marginal, with a thin margin of safety. Model cost is higher than for a chat-style service because a contract is long and legal Persian needs a larger model: about 4,535 toman per draft or review (about $0.017) on an assumed 30B-class model, gross margin 80–84% \[D\]. Revenue per customer is about 1.34M toman a month ($5.06) against 471.3M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 355 paying customers on paper and 411 with GPU nodes and hires counted \[D\]. The base case (200 customers at month 12, 900 at month 24) breaks even in month 16 with a peak cash need of 4,573M toman (about $17,237) and +353M a month at month 24, but cumulative cash is still −3,219M at month 24. The conservative case (60 / 250) never breaks even (−176M a month at month 24, cumulative cash −8,372M, about $31,559, a floor); the optimistic case (500 / 2,500) breaks even in month 11. Doubling the GPU price or halving customers each pushes base break-even to month 23 with a month-24 profit of only +53M and +16M, and cutting prices 30% leaves the base case slightly loss-making (−5M). Quality is the central risk: a model that mis-reads or invents a clause creates liability for a lawyer, I found no test of Persian legal-text accuracy for any open model, and the labour replaced is priced at the minimum-wage basis (no Iranian lawyer fee was found), which understates the value. Customer counts are hypotheses \[A\]. Tags: \[S\] sourced, \[D\] derived and recomputed by code, \[A\] assumption.

Pool: the American Bar Association reports more than 70,000 qualified lawyers in Iran (undated) and 31 areas in which lawyers can seek specialization certificates, contract law among them, under a directive of 16 January 2022 [S, americanbar.org legal-profession-in-iran-steps-toward-specialization, read 25 Oct 2026]; Wikipedia gives over 20,000 members for the Central Bar Association, citing a 2018 article, with 16 regional bar associations in all [S, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran\_Central\_Bar\_Association, read 25 Oct 2026]. No count of SMEs that buy legal drafting was found.

The user pastes or uploads a contract (or answers questions to draft one); the service flags missing or one-sided clauses, inconsistencies in names, dates and amounts, and ambiguous Persian wording, proposes replacement text from a clause library, and produces a clean draft with a short issue table, always with the source clause quoted. The labour replaced is a first read and issue list or a first draft: 45 minutes [A], valued here at 107,267 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance [D]), which understates a lawyer's time; no Iranian lawyer fee was found. The plans below charge 11,667–15,000 toman per document, 11–14% of that figure [D]. Reference points abroad: Luminance is listed at $10–$100 per user per month by a price-comparison site with no stated date, and Harvey publishes no price as of March 2026 [S, costbench.com/compare/harvey-ai-vs-luminance, read 25 Oct 2026]; the Solo plan below is about $1.70 a month.
Web app with Word import and export; a plug-in or email-forwarding route for lawyers; bar-association workshops and legal-education channels; referral by accountants and consultants for SMEs.

Free trial of 10 documents [A]; template and clause libraries by contract type; a human lawyer review option sold per document (not modelled); one customer-success person per 150 customers [A]; every output marked as a drafting aid that a qualified person must check. Monthly plan billed in toman, indexed to the exchange rate.

Monthly by number of drafts or reviews: Solo 450,000 toman (30 documents, about $1.70), Office 2,000,000 (150, about $7.54), Firm 7,000,000 (600, about $26.39) [A, no Iranian competitor price was found; a legal-AI app named Robovakil exists on a store page I could not read]. Mix 65% / 28% / 7% [A] gives ARPU 1,342,500 toman a month (about $5.06) [D].

A 30B-class open instruction model with Persian legal tuning and retrieval over a clause library; Persian legal templates reviewed by lawyers; a domestic GPU node (RTX 6000 Ada 48 GB, Sindad plan 150M toman a month [S]); 2 engineers, 1 lawyer or legal editor (80M gross [A]) and 1 customer-success hire.

Building and reviewing the clause library; evaluating outputs against lawyer-written answers; Word and PDF parsing of Persian contracts; keeping Iranian civil-code references correct; handling confidentiality and data residency.

Domestic GPU/cloud host; payment gateway (Zarinpal and similar, worst-case 1% fee [S, sources conflict: 0.05%–1%]); law firms or bar-association bodies as reviewers and distributors; legal publishers if a licence for statute text is needed (terms not verified).

Fixed: team 258.3M toman a month (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M + 1 legal editor at 80M gross [A] × 1.23 [S]), GPU node 150M, other infrastructure and encrypted document storage 15M, accounting 8M, marketing 40M = 471.3M toman a month (about $1,777) [D]; one-time setup 250M [A] (clause library and evaluation set). Variable: gateway 1% of revenue, an extra customer-success hire per 150 customers [A], an extra GPU node when load passes one node's capacity.
[D] (2 engineers at 50M + 1 customer-success at 30M + 1 legal editor at 80M gross, salaries [A]) × 1.23 employer insurance [S]
[S] Sindad GPU inference plan, listed 14 Sep 2026
[A] about 12,000 input (contract and clause-library context) plus about 3,000 output (issue table and redline text)

[D] 2,658.57 [S, A6000 vLLM benchmark, Llama-3.1-8B, 100 concurrent] × 0.8 (Ada vs A6000 and Persian token overhead, [A]) × 0.30 (a 30B-class model runs about 3.3 times slower than the 8B benchmark, [A]) × 30% average utilisation [A]
[D] 50% use [A] of the 30 / 150 / 600 quotas, weighted by plan mix

cost_model.x: One node covers about 536 customers at this usage [D: 33,077 ÷ (51.8 + 10 free-trial documents)], so GPU nodes step up with customers: 2 nodes in the base case at 900 customers and 5 in the optimistic case at 2,500 [D]. A 30B-class model may not fit one 48 GB card at full context with the batch sizes assumed, and I did not test it; a smaller model would cut cost and accuracy together.

revenue.x: Break-even is about 355 paying customers on the fixed-cost formula [D: 471.3M ÷ (1,342,500 × 0.99) = 354.6], and stepping through customer counts with the node and hires each needs gives 411 customers [D]. Customers ramp linearly from month 4 to the month-12 figure, then to the month-24 figure; the 250M setup falls in month 1.

Customer counts are [A]. For scale only, 900 accounts is 1.3% of the 70,000-plus lawyers reported by the American Bar Association [D, S above], although many accounts would be offices of several lawyers and some would be SMEs. In the conservative case cash is still falling at month 24, so the peak cash need is the month-24 position [D]. Cumulative cash at month 24 is −8,372M toman in the conservative case, −3,219M in the base case and +8,056M in the optimistic case [D]; the base-case peak of 4,573M came earlier, and payback is beyond month 24.

sensitivities.x: Churn is not in the cash rows (the customer path is fixed). At 5% monthly churn [A, a clause library and saved drafts are costly to move, but trust in the output may fail early] lifetime revenue per customer is about 26.6M toman [D: 1,342,500 × 0.99 ÷ 0.05]. Marketing cost per customer was not modelled separately; measure it in a pilot.

risks.x: Output quality and liability: a clause the model misreads, or a fabricated article reference, is the lawyer's liability; I found no benchmark of Persian legal text for open models, so the model size, the retrieval design and the human-review cost (one legal editor in the model) are all unverified.
Confidentiality: client contracts are confidential; many lawyers and firms will require domestic hosting and no training on their documents, which the model assumes but I could not confirm as a rule.

Regulatory standing of the bar: the judiciary controls licensing and bar governance, and the profession is under pressure [S, ibanet.org New-report-No-Defence, 4 Dec 2025, read 25 Oct 2026]; this may slow adoption through bar channels and raise caution about storing client files.

Substitutes: general chat assistants already draft contracts in Persian at no or low price; the value of this service depends on clause libraries, Iranian-law accuracy and Word workflow, which I could not compare.
Price level: Solo lawyers may value the tool at far more or far less than the 450,000 toman assumed; no Iranian lawyer fee or competitor price was found.
Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 [D]).

unverified.x: The number of practising lawyers today, SMEs that buy drafting help, and in-house legal departments; the counts found are undated or old.
Iranian lawyer fees for drafting and review, and prices of Iranian legal-AI tools (a store page for one app was blocked from automated reading).
Accuracy of any open 30B-class model on Persian contracts and Iranian civil law, real tokens per document, and whether such a model runs at the assumed throughput on the RTX 6000 Ada node.
Rules on storing and processing client documents outside the lawyer's own premises, and on non-lawyers offering contract drafting.
Licensing of statute and clause-library text.
Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.
Check run: all [D] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 25 Oct 2026.

32.verdict_md: Verdict: weak on these assumptions. Each answer needs retrieved articles and a larger model for legal Persian, so GPU cost is about 1,391 toman per answered question (about $0.0052) and gross margin is 62–71% \[D\], but the prices a citizen or a lawyer can plausibly pay per question are small. Revenue per customer is about 265,500 toman a month ($1.00) against 471.3M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 1,793 paying customers on paper and about 6,454 with GPU nodes and hires counted \[D\]. The base case (800 customers at month 12, 4,000 at month 24) never breaks even (−200M toman a month at month 24, cumulative cash −7,744M, about $29,190, a floor); the conservative case (200 / 1,000) loses 319M a month; only the optimistic case (2,500 / 12,000) breaks even, in month 17, with a peak cash need of 4,478M, +157M at month 24 and cumulative cash still −3,758M. Doubling the GPU price, cutting prices 30% or halving customers each deepens the base-case loss. The service would also compete with free access to the statutes themselves and with general chat assistants, and I found no test of how reliably a Persian model cites the right article without inventing one. Customer counts are hypotheses \[A\]. Tags: \[S\] sourced, \[D\] derived and recomputed by code, \[A\] assumption.

sections_md.risks:
- Accuracy and liability: a fabricated or outdated article reference can cause a wrong legal step; I found no benchmark of how reliably open models cite the right Iranian article, so model size, retrieval design and the human-review cost (one legal editor in the model) are unverified.
- Free substitutes: Iranian legislation was readable online without charge in 2015 \[S, 2015.index.okfn.org/place/iran/legislation, read 25 Oct 2026\], and domestic legal assistants already exist: a "RoboLegal" robot giving voice and text legal advice from Iranian cases was reported with no price and no date on the page (URL dated 17 Sep 2025) \[S, meatechwatch.com/2025/09/17/iran-launches-first-ai-powered-legal-robot-robolegal-to-expand-access-to-justice, read 25 Oct 2026\]; search also returned titles of a Robovakil app and a Parsivakil service, whose pages I could not read.
- Price level: citizens may not pay 3,000 toman a question when the substitute is free; lawyers may pay far more or less than 450,000 toman a month; no Iranian lawyer fee or competitor price was found.
- Regulatory standing: the judiciary controls licensing and bar governance and the profession is under pressure \[S, ibanet.org New-report-No-Defence, 4 Dec 2025, read 25 Oct 2026\]; whether a non-lawyer service may give answers that look like legal advice is not confirmed.
- Text rights and freshness: laws and rulings change often and the source text licence is unconfirmed; stale retrieval would produce wrong citations.
- Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 \[D\]).
sections_md.unverified:
- The number of citizens who look for legal information online, and the number of practising lawyers today (the 70,000-plus figure is undated).
- Iranian lawyer consultation fees and prices of domestic legal-AI tools (Robovakil and Parsivakil pages were blocked or title-only; RoboLegal has no price on its page).
- Accuracy of any open 30B-class model on Iranian statutes, real tokens per answer, and whether such a model runs at the assumed throughput on the RTX 6000 Ada node.
- Licence and machine-readable access to current statutes, regulations and rulings (the only source found is ten years old).
- Rules on non-lawyers giving legal answers, and on handling personal case details.
- Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.

Check run: all \[D\] figures above were recomputed by running the model in code on 25 Oct 2026.

33.title: Court ruling summarizer and precedent search
33.verdict_md: Verdict: marginal on these assumptions, and the decisive risk is data, not compute. GPU cost is about 1,965 toman per ruling summarized or searched (about $0.0074) and gross margin is 85–89% \[D\], but I found no evidence that Iranian court rulings are published in a form this service could collect, so the corpus, its licence and the 400M toman setup are unverified. Revenue per customer is about 955,000 toman a month ($3.60) against 471.3M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 499 paying customers on paper and 655 with the nodes and hires counted \[D\]. The base case (150 customers at month 12, 700 at month 24) breaks even only in month 24, with a peak cash need of 6,657M toman (about $25,093), +43M a month at month 24 and cumulative cash still −6,614M; the conservative case (50 / 200) never breaks even (−319M a month at month 24, cumulative cash −9,720M, a floor); the optimistic case (400 / 2,000) breaks even in month 14 with a peak cash need of 4,125M and +790M at month 24. Doubling the GPU price, cutting prices 30% or halving customers each removes the base-case break-even. The service also depends on a 30B-class model handling legal Persian, which I could not confirm. sections_md.risks:
- Corpus availability: in principle judgments are delivered in writing to the parties and their lawyers, but Revolutionary Courts often do not provide written copies, and the source I read describes delivery to parties only, not public publication \[S, osar.ch report on access to case files, 25 Mar 2019, read 25 Oct 2026; six years old\]. A corpus would then have to come from a judiciary licence or from lawyers uploading their own rulings, which raises confidentiality and quality problems. This could make the service impossible regardless of the model.
- Personal data: rulings name parties; automatic anonymisation errors are a legal risk; the applicable rules were not found.
- Accuracy and liability: a wrong summary of a holding, or a ruling shown as binding when it is not, harms the lawyer's client; I found no benchmark of Persian legal summarization by open models.
- Substitutes: lawyers already share rulings in professional channels and the judiciary may offer its own search to lawyers; I could not check either, and a state-run search would undercut any price.
- Regulatory standing of the bar: the judiciary controls licensing and the profession is under pressure \[S, ibanet.org New-report-No-Defence, 4 Dec 2025, read 25 Oct 2026\]; this may slow adoption through bar channels.
- Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 \[D\]).
sections_md.unverified:
- Whether any lawful, machine-readable source of Iranian court rulings exists, how many rulings it holds, and on what licence; the Supreme Court Wikipedia page does not say whether rulings are published.
- A current count of practising lawyers and of rulings issued per year (the 8 million cases a year figure dates from 2007 and counts cases, not written rulings).
- Prices of Iranian ruling-search tools and lawyer research fees.
- Accuracy of any open 30B-class model on Persian court rulings, real tokens per ruling, and throughput on the RTX 6000 Ada node.
- Rules on processing and anonymising judgments and on selling access to them.
- Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.

34.title: Rental and sale agreement generator
34.verdict_md: Verdict: weak on these assumptions. Compute is almost free (about 363 toman per agreement drafted, about $0.0014, gross margin 94–96% \[D\]), but the price an agency can plausibly pay per agreement is small, so revenue per customer is about 527,500 toman a month ($1.99) against 422.1M toman of fixed cost. Break-even needs about 808 paying customers on paper and 1,162 with a node and hires counted \[D\], against only 1,771 real-estate-agency companies in one web index \[S\]. No scenario breaks even in 24 months: the base case (80 customers at month 12, 300 at month 24) loses 302M toman a month at month 24 with cumulative cash −8,565M (about $32,284, a floor), the conservative case (30 / 120) loses 359M a month, and even the optimistic case (200 / 700) loses 167M a month with cumulative cash −7,213M. Doubling the GPU price, cutting prices 30% or halving customers each deepens the base-case loss. Lease registration and the 13-digit tracking code go through the national system and authorised agencies, so the product can draft but not register, and I found no API for it. A much leaner team might change the answer but the model keeps the standard four-person team. Customer counts are hypotheses \[A\]. Tags: \[S\] sourced, \[D\] derived and recomputed by code, \[A\] assumption.

35.title: Company registration and licence guidance assistant
35.verdict_md: Verdict: marginal at best, and weak in the base case. A guidance case costs about 9,070 toman of GPU time (about $0.034) and gross margin is 96–97% \[D\], but most customers would be founders who need one case and leave, so the customer path is mostly new buyers each month. Revenue per customer is about 1.30M toman a month ($4.89) against 471.3M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 367 paying customers on paper and 396 with the node and hires counted \[D\]. The base case (100 customers at month 12, 400 at month 24) does not break even within 24 months (−31M toman a month at month 24, cumulative cash −6,742M, about $25,412, a floor); the conservative case (40 / 150) loses 279M a month; the optimistic case (250 / 1,000) breaks even in month 15, with a peak cash need of 4,007M and +629M at month 24. Doubling the GPU price, cutting prices 30% or halving customers each deepens the base-case loss. The base case needs about 13% of the roughly 3,000 new limited companies registered each month, a ratio based on a single 2020 count \[D\]. Accuracy of guidance on Iranian licensing was not tested, and no domestic consultant fee was found. Customer counts are hypotheses \[A\]. sections_md.risks:
- Guidance accuracy: a wrong licence list or fee can delay a business or cost money; I found no benchmark of how reliably an open model answers Iranian registration and licensing questions, and rules change often.

- One-case customers: founders form a company once, so acquisition cost repeats for each case and the assumed price (450,000 toman) is untested; consultants who handle many cases are fewer and I found no count.
- Substitutes: consultants and lawyers who register companies, and official portals with their own instructions; I found no domestic fee for them, only a foreign-investor quote.
- Official systems: registration and licensing are handled by government offices and portals; I did not confirm what they publish or whether the product could submit anything on the founder's behalf.
- Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 \[D\]).

36.verdict_md: Verdict: viable but thin on these assumptions, and the case rests on a customer count I could not source. A tender reading is long (about 130,000 tokens), so GPU cost is about 39,302 toman per tender (about $0.148) and gross margin is 86–90% \[D\]; the plans charge 216,667–300,000 toman per tender against about 1.14M toman of reading time at the minimum wage \[D\]. Revenue per customer is about 3.46M toman a month ($13.04) against 471.3M toman of fixed cost, so break-even needs about 138 paying customers on paper and 149 with the node and hires counted \[D\]. The base case (100 customers at month 12, 350 at month 24) breaks even in month 15, with a peak cash need of 3,897M toman (about $14,689), +617M a month at month 24 and cumulative cash −607M; the conservative case (30 / 120) does not break even (−97M a month, cumulative cash −7,471M, a floor); the optimistic case (250 / 800) breaks even in month 9 with +1,674M at month 24.
