67.title: Employee survey analysis in Persian
67.verdict_md: Verdict: marginal and thin, with an unsized pool and light usage. The base case (300 paying firms at month 24) breaks even in month 17 but has not repaid its cash need by month 24 (cumulative −2,146M toman, about $8,090); the conservative case (90 firms) never breaks even and the optimistic case (750 firms) breaks even in month 10 \[D\]. Halving the customer counts also prevents break-even \[D\]. Firm counts are assumptions: I found no count of Iranian employers that run employee surveys. Employee surveys are usually run once or twice a year, so the model assumes firms use only 35% of their paid analyses and 10% monthly churn \[A\]; both are guesses. The compute node is 42.6% of fixed cost while loaded to under 5% \[D\], so a smaller GPU would help, which I did not model. Persian text quality is unverified for this task: embedding benchmarks exist (FaMTEB, below) but I found no benchmark on employee-comment theme coding. Employee comments are confidential, so customers may refuse to upload them.

68.title: Freelancer-to-project matcher with proposal help
68.verdict_md: Verdict: viable on the numbers, with willingness to pay and the project feed unproven. The base case (3,000 paying freelancers at month 24) breaks even in month 9 and earns +1,438M toman a month (about $5,420); the conservative case (1,000 freelancers) breaks even in month 17 and has not repaid its cash need by month 24 (cumulative −1,834M) \[D\]. Customer counts are assumptions; the only pool figure I found is a self-reported 50,000 freelancers on one Iranian platform in January 2018 \[S\], so the base case is 6.0% of that old figure \[D\]. The plan prices include a success fee on won contracts, which is assumed and not tested; I found no Iranian platform commission rate. The product cannot match anyone without a feed of open projects, and the platforms that hold the projects are its natural competitors, so the data supply is the main blocker. Prices per proposal are 12,000 to 15,000 toman (about $0.045 to $0.057) \[D\] against a general-purpose chatbot that freelancers can already use for free or for a few dollars \[A\]; I did not benchmark proposal quality.

69.title: Skills-gap and training recommender
69.verdict_md: Verdict: weak on the numbers. The base case (180 paying firms at month 24) breaks even in month 19 and is still 3,353M toman short in cumulative cash at month 24 (about $12,640); the conservative case (60 firms) never breaks even within 24 months (cumulative −6,531M), and the optimistic case (450 firms) breaks even in month 11 \[D\]. A GPU price rise, 30% lower prices, or half the customers each push the base case below break-even \[D\]. Firm counts are assumptions: I found no count of Iranian firms with a training function. The price per employee is tiny (about $0.07 an employee analysis \[D\]) because the model prices against the labour of an L&D specialist and not against LMS per-seat fees, so the service needs many firms to cover a team of three and a 150M toman GPU node that the load fills to about 12% \[D\]. The recommendations depend on a catalogue of Persian courses and on a skills taxonomy that I could not verify exists in usable form; without a catalogue the output is generic.

70.title: Performance review writer
70.verdict_md: Verdict: unprofitable on these assumptions. The base case (360 paying accounts at month 24) does not break even within 24 months and loses 69M toman a month at month 24 (cumulative −5,231M, about $19,720); the conservative case (120 accounts) also never breaks even (cumulative −7,137M), and the optimistic case (900 accounts) breaks even in month 15 but is still −1,174M cumulative at month 24 \[D\]. Account counts are assumptions: I found no count of Iranian firms that run formal performance reviews. Reviews are seasonal and the model assumes accounts use 30% of their paid drafts \[A\]. The average account pays 880,000 toman a month (about $3.32) \[D\], too little to carry a three-person team and a GPU node at the user counts I assumed; the compute load is about 3% of one node \[D\]. Foreign per-seat prices are low as well (Lattice $8 a user a month with a $4,000 minimum annual spend \[S\]), and a general chatbot costs nothing or $20 a month \[S\], so I see little room for a higher price. Persian quality of review text was not benchmarked.

71.title: Predictive maintenance from vibration and sensor data
71.verdict_md: Verdict: weak to marginal, and blocked first by hardware I could not source. The base case (120 paying sites at month 24) breaks even only in month 23 and earns +11M toman a month at month 24, with cumulative cash still −5,489M (about $20,690); the conservative case (45 sites) never breaks even (cumulative −8,357M), and the optimistic case (300 sites) breaks even in month 13 and ends at +1,053M cumulative \[D\]. Halving the customer count, cutting prices 30%, or doubling the GPU price each put the base case below break-even \[D\]. Site counts are assumptions: I found no count of Iranian plants with rotating machinery that would pay for monitoring (an undated headline mentions 43,000 active industrial units in 2019 \[S, eghtesadonline, page blocked, title only\]). The service needs vibration sensors that the customer must buy: vendor-blog prices are $150 to $350 for an entry-level wireless sensor, $400 to $800 with FFT, and $900 to $1,800 industrial-rated \[S, oxmaint.com, 28 May 2026, vendor blog, unverified\]; at 265,295 toman an entry sensor is 39.8M to 92.9M toman \[D\], about 133 to 310 months of the 300,000 toman a machine subscription here \[D\]. I did not find whether such sensors can be imported or built domestically, so hardware sourcing and price are unverified and not in the model. Detection quality on Iranian machines is unproven; the standard public benchmark (CWRU) shows accuracy dropping from about 95% to about 53% when the split stops leaking test information \[S, arxiv 2407.14625\].

72.title: Camera-based quality inspection
72.verdict_md: Verdict: marginal on the numbers and fragile, because the cost is dominated by GPU inference in the cloud. The base case (90 paying lines at month 24) breaks even in month 14 but has not repaid its cash need by month 24 (cumulative −1,369M toman, about $5,160), and it needs 12 GPU nodes by then, about 70% of monthly cost \[D\]. The conservative case (30 lines) never breaks even (cumulative −6,652M) and the optimistic case (240 lines) breaks even in month 8 and ends at +11,862M cumulative \[D\]. A doubled GPU price or 30% lower prices push the base case below break-even; half the customers still reaches break-even in month 22 with +6M a month at month 24 \[D\]. Line counts are assumptions: I found no count of Iranian production lines that would pay for inspection. 73.title: Standards and technical manual Q&A
73.verdict_md: Verdict: viable on the numbers, but the demand and the content rights are unproven. The base case (3,000 paying seats at month 24) breaks even in month 5, peaks at a cash need of 1,350M toman (about $5,090) and reaches +59,556M toman cumulative by month 24 \[D\]. The conservative case (900 seats) breaks even in month 9 and ends at +11,155M cumulative; the optimistic case (9,000 seats) breaks even in month 4 and ends at +197,107M \[D\]. Every sensitivity stays profitable: a doubled GPU price breaks even in month 6, prices 30% lower in month 6, and half the seats in month 7 \[D\]. The reason is the low unit cost: a question costs about 1,861 toman to serve (about $0.007) against about 47,674 toman of engineer time to find the same clause by hand \[D\]. Seat counts are assumptions: I found no count of Iranian engineering firms, factories or engineers who work from standards, so no pool supports them. The larger blockers are rights and quality. ISIRI (INSO) standards are sold documents, and I could not verify whether their text may be indexed and quoted in a commercial product; the Persian answer quality on technical clauses is also untested. Without a licence, the service can only index the customer's own copies and internal manuals, which fits the per-seat model but narrows the pitch.

sections_md.risks:
- Content rights: standards are copyrighted publications; without a licence from INSO or another publisher the product can index only the customer's own copies and manuals, which may be too narrow for the pitch.

- Seat pool: the number of firms that buy per-seat tools for engineers is unknown, and free general assistants compete on the same question.
- Data security: factories and defence-linked firms may refuse cloud upload of internal manuals, pushing demand to on-premises installs (see #99), which this model does not price.
- Price anchor: the foreign figure is a competitor's estimate of a vendor that does not publish prices; domestic prices were assumed and not tested.

74.title: Engineering report generator from test and simulation data
74.verdict_md: Verdict: viable on the numbers, but the customer pool is unsourced and the conservative case is only marginal. The base case (150 paying consultancies at month 24) breaks even in month 9, peaks at a cash need of 2,279M toman (about $8,589) and reaches +9,239M toman cumulative by month 24 \[D\]. The conservative case (45 consultancies) breaks even in month 20 but has not repaid its cash need by month 24 (cumulative −4,534M); the optimistic case (360) breaks even in month 6 and ends at +36,454M \[D\]. Every sensitivity stays profitable, with break-even in month 12 for a doubled GPU price, month 13 for prices 30% lower and month 14 for half the customers \[D\]. Compute is not the issue: one GPU node covers about 871 customers, so the base case runs on one node \[D\]. The risks are demand and trust. I found no count of Iranian engineering consultancies or test labs, so the customer counts are assumptions. The product writes the narrative and tables around numbers the engineer supplies; for certification-grade reports a signing engineer must still check every figure, and a language model that mis-states a number is a liability. The model prices one generic report type; each new report format (a test standard, a simulation template) needs engineering time that I covered only with the three-person team.

75.title: Energy-use optimizer for plants, greenhouses and buildings
75.verdict_md: Verdict: marginal on the numbers, and the value case rests on energy savings I could not price. The base case (75 paying sites at month 24) breaks even in month 12, peaks at a cash need of 2,392M toman (about $9,017) and reaches +3,491M toman cumulative by month 24 \[D\]. The conservative case (24 sites) reaches break-even only in month 24 and ends at −4,856M cumulative; the optimistic case (180 sites) breaks even in month 7 and ends at +19,763M \[D\]. Break-even in the base case slips to month 13 with doubled compute prices, month 14 with prices 30% lower and month 17 with half the sites \[D\]. The plans are priced at 116.5% to 186.5% of the cost of an engineer's hour per daily run \[D\], so labour saved does not justify them; the service must pay for itself through lower energy bills. At an assumed 5% saving, a Site S plan needs an energy bill of at least 160M toman a month (about $603) and Site L at least 1,000M (about $3,770) to break even for the customer \[D\], but I could not retrieve Iranian industrial electricity or gas tariffs, so I cannot say how many sites meet that. Site counts are assumptions, with no sourced pool. The savings-share fee named in the service list is not modelled; it is possible upside and would need metering the customer accepts as proof. The model runs on CPU servers, not GPUs.

76.verdict_md: Verdict: marginal-thin. The base case (90 paying plants at month 24) breaks even in month 14 but has not repaid its cash need by month 24 (cumulative −450M toman, about $1,696), with a peak cash need of 2,947M (about $11,107) \[D\]. The conservative case (30 plants) never breaks even and ends at −5,814M cumulative; the optimistic case (240 plants) breaks even in month 8 and ends at +12,343M \[D\]. In the base case, doubled compute prices move break-even to month 15, prices 30% lower to month 19 and half the plants to month 22, with month-24 profit of only +69M in the last case \[D\]. Plant counts are assumptions: I found no count of Iranian plants that run a maintenance store with usable part-usage history. The service also depends on data the customer must export from a maintenance or accounting system, and on a catalogue of alternative suppliers and equivalent parts that I could not find or price; the alternative-sourcing half of the product is therefore not costed. Price pressure is real because the larger plans cost only 16.1% of a planner's time per 100-part refresh \[D\], leaving little room to discount. The service runs on CPU servers, not GPUs.

77.title: Crop disease detection from phone photos
77.verdict_md: Verdict: viable on the numbers, but willingness to pay and diagnosis accuracy are unproven and the revenue per farmer is tiny. The base case (12,000 paying farmers at month 24) breaks even in month 8, peaks at a cash need of 1,989M toman (about $7,499) and reaches +29,029M toman cumulative by month 24 \[D\]. The conservative case (3,000 farmers) breaks even in month 15 but has not repaid its cash need by month 24 (cumulative −1,223M, about $4,610); the optimistic case (30,000) breaks even in month 5 and ends at +91,357M \[D\]. Every sensitivity stays profitable: a doubled GPU price breaks even in month 9, prices 30% lower in month 10 and half the farmers in month 12 \[D\]. Average revenue is only 570,000 toman a farmer a month (about $2.15) \[D\], so the model needs thousands of paying users, and I found no count of Iranian farmers who would pay for an app; the customer counts are assumptions. Usage is assumed at 50% of quota because disease problems are seasonal, and churn at 8% a month. Accuracy is the central risk: a competitor review says the best-known apps struggle with rare conditions and regional variants and should be treated as screening tools (flypix.ai, 9 Jun 2026 \[S\]), and I have no Iranian crop-image dataset. The model sends photos to our GPUs; one node serves about 4,700 farmers \[D\]. Spraying advice for pesticides sold in Iran needs a product list I did not find.

| Value proposition | The farmer photographs a leaf or fruit; the tool names the likely disease or pest, gives treatment and prevention steps in Persian, and logs the case by location so co-ops see outbreaks. The labour replaced is an agronomist consultation: 30 minutes \[A\], 71,512 toman at 143,023 toman an hour (1405 minimum wage loaded with 23% employer insurance \[D\]). 78.title: Irrigation and water-use advisor
78.verdict_md: Verdict: viable on the numbers, but it depends on a water saving I could not price and on farms having sensors or at least reliable field data. The base case (900 paying farms at month 24) breaks even in month 7, peaks at a cash need of 1,594M toman (about $6,009) and reaches +18,774M toman cumulative by month 24 \[D\]. The conservative case (300 farms) breaks even in month 13 and ends at +516M cumulative; the optimistic case (2,400 farms) breaks even in month 5 and ends at +64,163M \[D\]. Every sensitivity stays profitable: a doubled compute price breaks even in month 7, prices 30% lower in month 9 and half the farms in month 10 \[D\]. The plans are priced at 83.9% to 104.9% of the cost of an adviser's hour per hectare-month \[D\], so labour saved does not justify them alone; the value must come from lower water, pumping energy or higher yield. Iran's smart-irrigation programme gives context but no saving figure: about 10,000 hectares across 110 pilot projects, with no water-saving number stated (tvbrics.com, undated, read 28 Oct 2026 \[S\]). Farm counts are assumptions: I found no count of Iranian farms that would pay. The model runs on CPU servers, not GPUs; sensors, valves and controllers are the customer's cost and are not priced.

79.title: Construction cost estimator with inflation-indexed unit prices
79.verdict_md: Verdict: viable on the numbers, but the data behind the unit prices and the contractor pool are unverified. The base case (300 paying contractors at month 24) breaks even in month 8, peaks at a cash need of 1,904M toman (about $7,178) and reaches +15,476M toman cumulative by month 24 \[D\]. The conservative case (100 contractors) breaks even in month 16 but has not repaid its cash need by month 24 (cumulative −1,978M, about $7,456); the optimistic case (900) breaks even in month 5 and ends at +65,845M \[D\]. Every sensitivity stays profitable: a doubled GPU price and prices 30% lower both break even in month 10, and half the contractors in month 13 \[D\]. Free substitutes exist for the base data: an Android app with the official base unit price lists for 1396 to 1404 and their labour, machinery, material and transport breakdown has over 20,000 installs and a 4.6 rating from 272 ratings (Cafe Bazaar, read 28 Oct 2026 \[S\]), so the paid value has to come from inflation indexing, automatic quantity reading and tender-specific pricing. Because the official price lists lag real market prices in a high-inflation economy, an index built from current supplier quotes would be the real product; I found no source for such quotes and the model prices one data analyst at 40M toman a month to curate them. Contractor counts are assumptions.

80.title: Procurement quote comparison assistant
80.verdict_md: Verdict: viable on the numbers, but the buyer pool is unsourced and the conservative case does not repay its cash need. The base case (360 paying purchasing teams at month 24) breaks even in month 9, peaks at a cash need of 1,822M toman (about $6,867) and reaches +8,975M toman cumulative by month 24 \[D\]. The conservative case (120 teams) breaks even in month 18 but ends at −2,895M cumulative (about $10,912); the optimistic case (900) breaks even in month 6 and ends at +34,001M \[D\]. Every sensitivity stays profitable but slower: a doubled GPU price breaks even in month 11, prices 30% lower in month 13 and half the teams in month 14, with +500M a month at month 24 in the last case \[D\]. I found no count of Iranian purchasing teams and no domestic price for a comparable tool (the searches returned only international RFQ and lead-generation products with no prices), so the customer counts and prices are assumptions. Quotes in Iran often arrive as phone photos, PDF invoices and chat messages with prices that expire within days; reading them accurately and keeping terms such as prepayment, validity and delivery comparable is the hard part, and an extraction error becomes a purchasing error.

81.title: Used-car price estimator and listing-fraud checker
81.verdict_md: Verdict: viable on the numbers, but it depends on price data I could not find and on a few large marketplace customers. The base case (360 paying dealers and marketplaces at month 24) breaks even in month 7, peaks at a cash need of 1,658M toman (about $6,250) and reaches +23,239M toman cumulative by month 24 \[D\]. The conservative case (120 customers) breaks even in month 13 and ends at +1,730M cumulative; the optimistic case (900) breaks even in month 5 and ends at +71,113M \[D\]. Every sensitivity stays profitable: a doubled GPU price breaks even in month 8, prices 30% lower in month 8 and half the customers in month 10 \[D\]. Revenue is concentrated: the Marketplace plan is 10% of customers \[A\] but 53% of revenue \[D: 6,000,000 of 11,400,000 toman\], so losing a few large accounts would change the result; it also has the lowest gross margin, 79.6% \[D\]. A price model needs a history of Iranian asking and sold prices, which marketplaces hold and I found no licensed source for; the pages I found gave only market-level figures (2025 new-vehicle sales of 1,192,969 units, BSCB via bestsellingcarsblog.com, 27 Jan 2026 \[S\]) and no used-car volume. Customer counts are assumptions. In a market where car prices move with the exchange rate, estimates go stale within days, and a fraud flag that wrongly accuses a seller is a reputational risk.

82.title: Property valuation and listing-copy generator
82.verdict_md: Verdict: viable on the numbers, but it is a low-price product for a pool I could not size, and its customers have cheap general-purpose substitutes. The base case (3,500 paying agents at month 24) breaks even in month 7, peaks at a cash need of 1,809M toman (about $6,819) and reaches +25,971M toman cumulative by month 24 \[D\]. The conservative case (1,000 customers) breaks even in month 14 and ends at only +191M cumulative, so it is barely positive after two years; the optimistic case (10,000) breaks even in month 5 and ends at +94,928M \[D\]. Every sensitivity stays profitable: a doubled GPU price breaks even in month 8, prices 30% lower in month 9 and half the customers in month 11 \[D\]. Plans cost 3,000 to 6,000 toman a task, 4.2% to 8.4% of the 71,512 toman an agent's 30 minutes costs \[D\], so the price is small against the labour replaced, but general-purpose writing tools already list at $0 to $99 a month (ChatGPT free to $20, Jasper Pro $69 per user, Writesonic Starter $99; eesel.ai, 7 May 2026 \[S\]) and I found no Iranian price. I found no national count of Iranian estate agents (only regional figures of 'real estate consulting units' in two provinces, Iran International, 13 Sep 2021 \[S\], definition unclear), so 3,500 customers is an assumption. The valuation half needs sale and rental price history that marketplaces hold and I found no licensed source; the listing-copy half does not and could be sold alone. A valuation shown to a buyer or seller carries accuracy and liability risk.

83.title: Classifieds moderation and spam detection API
83.verdict_md: Verdict: viable on the numbers, but the customer pool is small and unsourced, and the biggest classified sites probably moderate in-house. The base case (120 paying sites at month 24) breaks even in month 6, peaks at a cash need of 1,333M toman (about $5,026) and reaches +17,812M toman cumulative by month 24 \[D\]. The conservative case (40 sites) breaks even in month 11 and ends at +1,371M cumulative; the optimistic case (300) breaks even in month 5 and ends at +54,824M \[D\]. Every sensitivity stays profitable: a doubled GPU price breaks even in month 9, prices 30% lower in month 9 and half the customers in month 9 \[D\]. Compute is the main cost: 8 GPU nodes at month 24 are about 69% of that month's cost \[D\], and the Large plan has a gross margin of only 56.4% \[D\], so heavy customers earn less per ad. Revenue is concentrated: the Large plan is 5% of customers \[A\] but 46% of revenue \[D\]. The pool is the weak point: I found no count of Iranian classified or marketplace sites. The one volume figure found is for Divar alone, 139.7 million new ads a year, about 11.6 million a month \[D\] (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Divar\_(website), undated annual report, read 31 Oct 2026 \[S\]). The base case assumes the 120 customers check about 39.4 million ads a month in total \[D: 120 × 328 thousand\], more than three times Divar's volume, so it needs many mid-size sites rather than one giant; a site of Divar's size is likely to build its own moderation. Customer counts are assumptions. Accuracy on Persian text, local slang, price spam and prohibited-goods rules is unproven, and wrongly blocking a seller's ad is a customer-visible error.

84.title: Delivery route optimizer for small fleets
84.verdict_md: Verdict: viable on the numbers, but the customer pool is unsourced, the prices rest on a labour estimate I could not check, and free map-app routing is the real competitor. The base case (1,500 paying fleets at month 24) breaks even in month 5, peaks at a cash need of 1,020M toman (about $3,846) and reaches +39,721M toman cumulative by month 24 \[D\]. The conservative case (500 fleets) breaks even in month 8 and ends at +9,524M cumulative; the optimistic case (4,000) breaks even in month 4 and ends at +114,107M \[D\]. Every sensitivity stays profitable: a doubled server price breaks even in month 6, prices 30% lower in month 6 and half the customers in month 7 \[D\]. The workload is route solving on CPU servers, so compute is small: 6 CPU servers at month 24 are about 17% of that month's cost \[D\]. The price anchor is foreign: OptimoRoute lists $39 (Lite) and $49 (Pro) per driver per month (demo.upperinc.com, updated 23 Mar 2026, competitor blog \[S\]); the plans here charge 180,000 to 250,000 toman (about $0.68 to $0.94) per vehicle, about 2% of that \[D\], so the model assumes Iranian buyers will pay roughly one fiftieth of the foreign price, which is \[A\]. Revenue is concentrated: the Fleet plan is 5% of customers \[A\] but 42% of revenue \[D\]. I found no count of Iranian couriers, delivery shops or fleets (an AloPeyk page I tried was not retrievable), so customer counts are assumptions. Route quality depends on road, traffic and address data from a domestic map provider, whose price and licence terms I could not find.

sections_md.canvas:
| Block | Content |
| --- | --- |
| Customer segments | (a) Shops and small businesses with up to 5 delivery vehicles (Shop plan). (b) Courier companies and distributors with about 30 vehicles (Courier plan). (c) Large fleets with about 200 vehicles (Fleet plan). Pool: no count of Iranian delivery vehicles or fleets was found; 1,500 paying customers at month 24 is \[A\]. |
| Value proposition | The customer uploads or enters the day's stops, vehicles and time windows and gets an ordered route for each vehicle, estimated arrival times and updates when an order is added. 85.title: Retail demand and stock forecasting
85.verdict_md: Verdict: viable on the numbers only if a very large number of small shops pay, and the model leans on an optimistic support ratio. The base case (8,000 paying retailers at month 24) breaks even in month 6, peaks at a cash need of 1,114M toman (about $4,199) and reaches +30,741M toman cumulative by month 24 \[D\]. The conservative case (2,000 retailers) breaks even in month 13 and ends at +2,851M cumulative; the optimistic case (25,000) breaks even in month 4 and ends at +108,199M \[D\]. Every sensitivity stays profitable: a doubled server price breaks even in month 6, prices 30% lower in month 8 and half the customers in month 8 \[D\]. ARPU is only 735,000 toman a month (about $2.77) \[D\], so the business needs about 414 paying customers before it breaks even and a lifetime value of about 11.8M toman (about $44.5) per customer limits what can be spent to win each one \[D\]. The main cost is support, not compute: at 1 support person per 200 customers \[A\] the base case employs 40 support staff at month 24, about 71% of that month's cost of 2,084M, while 3 CPU servers are about 7% \[D\]; a looser ratio would change the result, and I did not stress it. Foreign tools list at $49 a month and up (Prediko from $49, Inventory Planner Essentials $119.99, Cin7 Core $349; ud.hk, prices as of 11 Aug 2026 \[S\]); the Small plan here, 300,000 toman (about $1.13), is about 2% of the cheapest \[D\]. The base case equals 2.6% of the 308,000 sellers Digikala reported for FY1401 \[S, D\], but sellers on one marketplace are not the same as shops with stock records, and I found no count of Iranian retail shops or how many keep digital stock data. Forecast accuracy depends on clean sales history that small shops often lack.

sections_md.risks:
- Acquisition cost: ARPU is about $2.77 a month and lifetime value about $44.5 \[D\], so any real acquisition cost above a few dollars per shop erases the margin.
- Support load: the model assumes 1 support person per 200 customers \[A\], and support is about 71% of base month-24 cost \[D\]; small shops needing hand-holding with data upload would break this.
- Data quality: many small shops have no digital sales history, which limits who can use a forecast.
- Free or bundled substitutes: shop-management and marketplace seller tools may add forecasting at no charge.
- Forecast value: an inflationary market with price shocks and supply gaps makes demand history a weak guide; accuracy is unproven.
- Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 \[D\]).

86.title: Insurance risk scoring and quote assistant
86.verdict_md: Verdict: viable on the numbers, but thin in the conservative case, and it depends on insurers' product and pricing data that I could not verify. The base case (500 paying agents, agencies and insurers at month 24) breaks even in month 8, peaks at a cash need of 1,864M toman (about $7,027) and reaches +24,748M toman cumulative by month 24 \[D\]. The conservative case (150 customers) breaks even in month 14 and ends at only +642M cumulative; the optimistic case (1,000) breaks even in month 5 and ends at +64,118M \[D\]. Every sensitivity stays profitable: a doubled GPU price breaks even in month 9, prices 30% lower in month 9 and half the customers in month 12 \[D\]. Revenue is concentrated: the Insurer plan is 2% of customers \[A\], about 10 insurers in the base case \[D\], but 34% of revenue \[D: 3,000,000 of 8,700,000 toman\]. Iran had 25 active insurers in 2014, all but one private, and more than 25 regulated companies in 2018 (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central\_Insurance\_of\_Iran, read 31 Oct 2026 \[S\]), so the base case needs about 40% of the insurers \[D: 10 of 25, using the 2014 count\], which is optimistic; I found no count of Iranian insurance agents. Free tools exist: insurers' own AI tools are free to agents elsewhere (ud.hk, 20 Oct 2026 \[S\]) and general chat tools cost $20 to $25 a user. A quote tool needs each insurer's rate tables or API, and Iranian premiums for compulsory lines are set by the regulator \[A, unverified\], which limits what a model can add. A wrong quote or risk score is a liability for the customer and the service.

87.title: Domestic-travel itinerary planner
87.verdict_md: Verdict: marginal to weak, and the result rests on a commission rate I could not verify. In this model a customer is one booked trip in a month, not a subscriber, so every month's trips must be won again \[A\]. The base case (2,000 booked trips a month at month 24) breaks even in month 12, peaks at a cash need of 3,014M toman (about $11,360) and reaches +5,898M toman cumulative by month 24 \[D\]. The conservative case (500 trips a month) reaches monthly break-even only in month 24 and is at -6,478M cumulative; the optimistic case (6,000) breaks even in month 6 and ends at +39,420M \[D\]. A doubled GPU price moves base break-even to month 14, prices 30% lower to month 15 and half the trips to month 16 \[D\]. Income here is a commission on bookings made through the plan: 8% of a 6M toman trip, 7% of 25M and 6% of 100M \[A\], against OTA benchmarks of about 10% to 30% paid by hotels (Booking.com 10-20%, Expedia 15-30%, Airbnb 15.5%, Trip.com 10-25%; smartorder.ai, benchmarks, modified 1 Sep 2026 \[S\]). I found no Iranian commission rate, and the service would sit between a traveller and hotels, tour sellers and ticket sellers that already run their own large platforms. The Iranian online travel market is estimated at $2,037.7M in 2025 (IMARC, a vendor estimate, read 31 Oct 2026 \[S\]); the base case's booked value is about $1.4M a year \[D\], about 0.07% of that, so scale is not the question; winning the traveller's booking and getting access to supplier availability and prices is. The itinerary text is cheap to produce; the booking link is what earns money.

88.title: Guesthouse and hotel dynamic pricing with review replies
88.verdict_md: Verdict: marginal. The base case (1,800 paying properties at month 24) breaks even in month 10, peaks at a cash need of 2,000M toman (about $7,538) and reaches +9,819M toman cumulative by month 24 \[D\]. The conservative case (500 properties) breaks even in month 19 but is still at -3,688M cumulative at month 24, so it has not recovered its losses in two years; the optimistic case (5,000) breaks even in month 6 and ends at +43,562M \[D\]. Every sensitivity stays profitable on a monthly basis but slowly: a doubled GPU price breaks even in month 12, prices 30% lower in month 13 and half the customers in month 14 \[D\]. ARPU is only 1,436,000 toman a month (about $5.41) \[D\], lifetime value is about 27.2M toman (about $102.6) \[D\], and support staff at 1 per 150 customers \[A\] are about 45% of base month-24 cost \[D\]. Foreign tools are priced far higher (Smartpricing from EUR111 a month, smartness.com, modified 1 Sep 2026 \[S\], about 33M toman at an assumed 300,000 toman per EUR; the Hotel plan here is about 6% of that \[D\]), and the other vendors publish no price. I found no count of Iranian hotels, guesthouses or ecolodges (a 2018 hospitality article gave none), so customer counts are assumptions, and I could not check how many properties set prices actively or how many sell through channels that expose competitor rates. Customers must pay for pricing advice when many properties price by feel and occupancy depends on seasons, holidays and travel conditions that a model cannot see.

89.title: Restaurant demand forecasting and menu repricing
89.verdict_md: Verdict: marginal. The base case (1,800 paying restaurant customers at month 24) breaks even in month 8, peaks at a cash need of 1,486M toman (about $5,602) and reaches +9,992M toman cumulative by month 24 \[D\]. The conservative case (500 customers) breaks even in month 17 but is still at -2,080M cumulative at month 24; the optimistic case (5,000) breaks even in month 5 and ends at +40,978M \[D\]. Every sensitivity stays profitable on a monthly basis but slowly: a doubled server price breaks even in month 10, prices 30% lower in month 11 and half the customers in month 13 \[D\]. ARPU is only 1,265,000 toman a month (about $4.77) \[D\] and lifetime value about 24.8M toman (about $93.6) \[D\]. The cost that matters is support, not compute: at 1 support person per 150 customers \[A\] the base case employs 12 at month 24, about 56% of that month's cost of 787M, while 1 CPU node is about 6% \[D\]. The base case serves about 4,590 outlets \[D: 1,800 customers × 2.55\], which is 21% of the 21,670 cafe listings counted in Oct 2025 (poidata.io, a listing-data vendor \[S\]); I found no count of restaurants, so the pool is unsourced. Many outlets keep no digital sales records, and a price suggestion that is wrong in a market with fast cost inflation can hurt the owner. I found no foreign or domestic competitor price for restaurant forecasting.

90.title: Import-export documentation and tariff-code assistant (sanctions-sensitive)
90.verdict_md: Verdict: viable on the numbers, with legal and data blockers that the model does not price. The base case (1,200 paying customers at month 24) breaks even in month 8, peaks at a cash need of 1,971M toman (about $7,428) and reaches +18,335M toman cumulative by month 24 \[D\]. The conservative case (400 customers) breaks even in month 15 but is still at -582M cumulative at month 24; the optimistic case (3,500) breaks even in month 5 and ends at +71,357M \[D\]. Every sensitivity stays profitable on a monthly basis: a doubled GPU price breaks even in month 10, prices 30% lower in month 11 and half the customers in month 13 \[D\]. ARPU is 2,870,000 toman a month (about $10.82) \[D\] and lifetime value about 69.8M toman (about $263) \[D\]. The cost that matters is compute and support together: at month 24 the base case runs 2 GPU nodes (about 33% of that month's cost of 904M) and 6 added support staff (about 24%) \[D\]. Customer counts are \[A\]: I found no count of Iranian importers, exporters or customs brokers, so the pool is unsourced. The blockers are (1) tariff-code and duty accuracy, because Iranian duties are a 4% minimum plus a trading profit set by the Council of Ministers and the schedule has 8,357 tariff lines as of 2020 \[S\], so a wrong code or a stale rate can cost the customer money and the service has no confirmed rate feed; (2) sanctions: the United States keeps comprehensive sanctions on Iran apart from specific licences, and General License X of 22 June 2026 covered only oil, petrochemical and related shipping, insurance and payment transactions and was due to expire on 21 August 2026 \[S\], so the service must run only on domestic hosting and models, must not draft documents that hide the origin, destination or parties of a shipment, and may be asked by customers to do so; (3) the customer remains legally responsible for the declaration, so liability sits with the user but disputes would reach the provider.

sections_md.risks:
- Wrong code or stale duty rate: the schedule has 8,357 tariff lines (2020) and duty includes a trading profit set by the Council of Ministers \[S\]; a wrong answer costs the customer duty or a penalty. Vendor-reported AI first-pass accuracy of 93-96% against 90-95% for specialist brokers (camtomx.com, undated, vendor \[S\]) is not Iranian evidence.
- Sanctions exposure: Iran remains under comprehensive US sanctions except for specific licences \[S, GL X, 22 Jun 2026, expiry 21 Aug 2026, status after that not checked\]. The service must use no foreign cloud or model, and customers may ask for documents that conceal parties or origin; screening and refusal rules are a cost and a churn risk.
- Data access: no confirmed source for official tariff and rate updates or for permit rules by code.
- Broker substitution: customs brokers already prepare declarations and bundle classification in the per-entry fee \[S, camtomx.com\]; a broker-office plan only works if brokers adopt the tool rather than treat it as a threat.
- Liability: the user signs the declaration, but disputes over a suggested code would reach the provider; terms of service and professional insurance are unpriced.
- Rial drift: toman prices need monthly indexing (the dollar rate rose 30.6% from 24 Aug to 17 Oct 2026 \[D\]).

- Whether OFAC General License X was extended past 21 August 2026, and how sanctions law applies to each customer's trade.
- Zarinpal fee and VAT, as in #1.

91.title: Persian blog and social content writer with brand voice
91.verdict_md: Verdict: viable on the numbers, with a thin ARPU and an unproven quality edge. The base case (3,500 paying customers at month 24) breaks even in month 7, peaks at a cash need of 1,570M toman (about $5,919) and reaches +27,403M toman cumulative by month 24 \[D\]. The conservative case (1,000 customers) breaks even in month 13 and is at +1,371M cumulative at month 24; the optimistic case (10,000) breaks even in month 5 and ends at +96,303M \[D\]. Every sensitivity stays profitable: a doubled GPU price breaks even in month 8, prices 30% lower in month 8 and half the customers in month 10 \[D\]. ARPU is 1,470,000 toman a month (about $5.54) \[D\] and lifetime value about 23.4M toman (about $88) \[D\]. Costs scale with usage, not with the team: at month 24 the base case runs 4 GPU nodes (about 36% of that month's cost of 1,660M) and 14 added support staff (about 31%) \[D\]. Customer counts are \[A\]; the base case is 1.1% of the 308,000 sellers Digikala reported for FY1401 \[S\] only as a scale marker, because the buyer pool (small shops, marketers, agencies) is unsourced. The blockers are Persian text quality from a 30B-class open model and its licence (not checked), the fact that general chat tools already write Persian at low or no cost (not priced here), and that Instagram and Telegram, where much of the content is posted, are subject to filtering rules that I did not verify. Foreign tools are priced at $69 (Jasper Pro, monthly) and $29 (Copy.ai Chat) per user \[S, costbench.com, June 2026, third-party\]; the Solo plan here is $2.26.

92.title: Video subtitling and dubbing pipeline (speech-to-text, translation, speech synthesis)
92.verdict_md: Verdict: marginal, and weaker than its headline break-even suggests. The base case (3,500 paying customers at month 24) breaks even in month 13, peaks at a cash need of 2,600M toman (about $9,801) and reaches only +2,515M toman cumulative by month 24 \[D\]. The conservative case (1,000 customers) first shows a profit in month 23 but loses 99M in month 24 when a new GPU node is added and is at -5,317M cumulative \[D\]; the optimistic case (10,000) breaks even in month 7 and ends at +23,240M \[D\]. A doubled GPU price or prices 30% lower each push the base case to no break-even within 24 months, and only halving customers still breaks even (month 16) \[D\]. ARPU is 955,000 toman a month (about $3.60) \[D\] and lifetime value about 13.2M toman (about $50) \[D\]. Compute is the cost that matters: gross margin by plan falls from 63.9% to 40.4%, and at month 24 the base case runs 8 GPU nodes, about 46% of that month's cost of 2,581M, plus 14 added support staff, about 20% \[D\]. Customer counts are \[A\]: I found no count of Iranian video creators, schools or channels (Aparat reports 60M+ monthly users but no creator count \[S\]), so the pool is unsourced. The blockers are licence and quality of the speech-synthesis step, because the Persian voice models I found are non-commercial (one CC-BY-NC 4.0, one under the Coqui public licence, which restricts commercial use \[S\]), and dubbing quality in Persian is unproven. Foreign dubbing tools charge about $0.24 to $2.44 per video minute \[S, perso.ai, 23 Oct 2026, vendor page, Persian support not stated\], while the plans here are $0.015 to $0.025 a minute; the low price is \[A\] and is what keeps margins thin.

93.title: Poster and banner generator with correct Persian typography
93.verdict_md: Verdict: viable on the numbers, with a licence check and a typography-quality test still open. The base case (4,500 paying customers at month 24) breaks even in month 7, peaks at a cash need of 1,592M toman (about $6,003) and reaches +23,344M toman cumulative by month 24 \[D\]. The conservative case (1,400 customers) breaks even in month 13 and is at +1,361M cumulative at month 24; the optimistic case (12,000) breaks even in month 5 and ends at +79,381M \[D\]. Every sensitivity stays profitable: a doubled GPU price breaks even in month 10, prices 30% lower in month 10 and half the customers in month 10 \[D\]. ARPU is 1,200,000 toman a month (about $4.52) \[D\] and lifetime value about 16.4M toman (about $62) \[D\]. GPU time is the main cost: at month 24 the base case runs 8 nodes, about 50% of that month's cost of 2,388M, plus 18 added support staff, about 28% \[D\]. Customer counts are \[A\]; the base case is 1.5% of the 308,000 sellers Digikala reported for FY1401 \[S\] only as a scale marker, because the buyer pool is unsourced. The design that makes the service credible is that Persian text is set by a layout engine in licensed fonts, not drawn by the image model, so correct joining, right-to-left order and numerals do not depend on the model; I did not test this. Licences matter: SDXL and SD 3.5 fall under the Stability AI Community License with a revenue threshold whose figure I did not find, FLUX.1 schnell is Apache 2.0 and FLUX.1 dev is non-commercial \[S, eastondev.com, 3 Jun 2026\]. Canva Pro costs $18 a month per person ($180 a year) \[S, piktochart.com, mid-2026, third-party\] against the Starter plan here at $1.88; whether Canva handles Persian well and is usable from Iran was not verified.

94.verdict_md: Verdict: marginal, because ARPU is very low and support dominates cost. The base case (6,000 paying customers at month 24) breaks even in month 9, peaks at a cash need of 1,894M toman (about $7,138) and reaches +11,566M toman cumulative by month 24 \[D\]. The conservative case (2,000 customers) breaks even in month 16 but is still at -1,630M cumulative at month 24; the optimistic case (18,000) breaks even in month 5 and ends at +52,186M \[D\]. Every sensitivity stays profitable on a monthly basis but slowly: a doubled GPU price breaks even in month 11, prices 30% lower in month 13 and half the customers in month 14 \[D\]. ARPU is 550,000 toman a month (about $2.07) \[D\] and lifetime value about 6.6M toman (about $25) \[D\]. Compute is cheap (1,457 toman a script plan \[D\]); the cost that matters is support: at 1 support person per 300 customers \[A\] the base case adds 20 at month 24, about 47% of that month's cost of 1,554M, while 3 GPU nodes are about 29% \[D\]. Customer counts are \[A\]: I found no count of Iranian short-video creators, so the pool is unsourced, and 6,000 paying creators is a claim I cannot support from data. The product writes text only, so the main blockers are Persian script quality, hook and trend knowledge that the model does not have, and that free chat assistants already do this task (not priced here). A foreign anchor: Opus Clip, a video-clipping tool, charges $15 to $29 a month \[S, costbench.com, checked 29 Oct 2026, third-party\]; it does a different job, and I found no foreign price for a Persian script planner.

95.title: Persian news and brand-mention monitoring with summaries
95.verdict_md: Verdict: viable on the numbers, but the product depends on collecting data that the main Iranian news sites may not allow. The base case (1,200 paying customers at month 24) breaks even in month 8, peaks at a cash need of 1,910M toman (about $7,201) and reaches +25,885M toman cumulative by month 24 \[D\]. The conservative case (400 customers) breaks even in month 14 and is at +1,515M cumulative at month 24; the optimistic case (3,000) breaks even in month 5 and ends at +80,659M \[D\]. Every sensitivity stays profitable: a doubled GPU price breaks even in month 9, prices 30% lower in month 10 and half the customers in month 12 \[D\]. ARPU is 3,770,000 toman a month (about $14.21) \[D\] and lifetime value about 92.8M toman (about $350) \[D\]. Support is the cost that matters: at 1 support person per 100 customers \[A\], because PR teams need alert tuning, the base case adds 12 at month 24, about 45% of that month's cost of 978M, while 1 GPU node is about 15% \[D\]. Customer counts are \[A\]: I found no count of Iranian PR teams, agencies or brands that monitor media, so the pool is unsourced. The main blocker is data access: nearly every Iranian news and tech site I tried to fetch during this research blocked automated access through robots rules \[S, observed across this report\], so collection would rely on licensed feeds, agency partnerships or permitted APIs that I could not confirm; Instagram and Telegram coverage depends on access that was not verified either. Foreign price anchors are Brand24 at $199 to $499 a month for 2,000 to 40,000 mentions and Awario at $29 to $149 \[S, authoritytech.io, prices captured 9 Sep 2026, competitor blog\]; none of them is shown to cover Persian well. The Single brand plan here is $4.52.

96.title: Persian OCR API (printed, handwritten, ID and card images)
96.verdict_md: Verdict: viable on the numbers but compute-bound, so the result depends on the GPU price and on a few high-volume accounts. The base case (600 paying accounts at month 24) breaks even in month 7, peaks at a cash need of 1,695M toman (about $6,389) and reaches +36,372M toman cumulative by month 24 \[D\]. The conservative case (200 accounts) breaks even in month 11 and is at +6,150M cumulative at month 24; the optimistic case (1,500) breaks even in month 4 and ends at +107,586M \[D\]. The sensitivities show the exposure: a doubled GPU price means no break-even within 24 months, a peak cash need of 17,778M and a month-24 loss of 1,286M; prices 30% lower break even in month 13 and half the accounts in month 10 \[D\]. ARPU is 20,300,000 toman a month (about $76.52) \[D\] and lifetime value about 604M toman (about $2,278) \[D\]. The base case processes about 19.7M pages a month at month 24 \[D\], needs 39 GPU nodes, about 77% of that month's cost of 7,616M, while 4 added support staff are about 2% \[D\]. Enterprise accounts are 5% of customers \[A\] but 49% of revenue and use 76% of the pages \[D\], at a gross margin of 29.1% \[D\]. Account counts and volumes are \[A\]: I found no count of Iranian developers or back offices that need OCR, so the pool is unsourced. On a public Persian benchmark of 6,669 printed lines and 6,669 handwritten pages \[S, Reza2kn dataset, undated, table has copy errors\], a 666M-parameter model (Bina 0.1 Koochik) scored a handwriting word error rate of 11.41% and a closed-API model (Gemini 3.5 Flash) 33.95%, while Tesseract scored 89%; the licences of these open models were not stated, so the commercial right to run them is unconfirmed. Google's Enterprise OCR costs $1.50 per 1,000 pages ($0.60 above 5M pages) \[S, 24 Oct 2026\], against $3.02, $2.26 and $1.51 per 1,000 pages here. ID and card images are personal data, which adds storage and consent duties that I did not research.

97.title: Domestically hosted LLM API billed in rials
97.verdict_md: Verdict: viable on the numbers, with thinner exposure to compute than image or OCR services, but the demand case is access, not price. The base case (600 paying accounts at month 24) breaks even in month 8, peaks at a cash need of 1,828M toman (about $6,890) and reaches +20,034M toman cumulative by month 24 \[D\]. The conservative case (200 accounts) breaks even in month 14 and is only +504M cumulative at month 24; the optimistic case (1,500) breaks even in month 5 and ends at +64,856M \[D\]. The sensitivities hold up: a doubled GPU price still breaks even in month 12 and earns +963M a month at month 24; prices 30% lower break even in month 11; half the accounts in month 12 \[D\]. ARPU is 8,525,000 toman a month (about $32.13) \[D\] and lifetime value about 139.6M toman (about $526) at 6% monthly churn \[D\]. The compute cost is 92,698 toman per million tokens (about $0.35) \[D\] against plan prices of 300,000, 240,000 and 200,000 toman (about $1.13, $0.90 and $0.75). Foreign hosts of the same 8B-class model list $0.02 to $0.22 per million tokens \[S, pricepertoken.com, page updated 3 Jul 2026\], so the domestic price is roughly 3 to 56 times higher \[D\]; it only sells to developers who cannot pay foreign providers in dollars or whose data may not leave Iran, and I did not verify how many that is \[A\]. Base-case month 24 uses 12 GPU nodes, about 77% of that month's cost of 2,352M, and 4 added support staff, about 6% \[D\]. Account counts are \[A\]: no count of Iranian developers or startups buying LLM API access was found, and no domestic LLM API price was found. The open model, its Persian quality and its commercial licence are not checked here.

98.verdict_md: Verdict: marginal. The base case (600 paying accounts at month 24) breaks even in month 13, peaks at a cash need of 2,758M toman (about $10,396) and reaches only +4,206M toman cumulative by month 24 \[D\]. The conservative case (200 accounts) breaks even in month 19 but is still -4,847M cumulative at month 24; the optimistic case (1,500) breaks even in month 7 and ends at +26,082M \[D\]. The sensitivities show little margin: a doubled GPU price means no break-even within 24 months and a month-24 loss of 304M a month; prices 30% lower break even in month 19 with only +84M a month at month 24; half the accounts break even in month 17 \[D\]. ARPU is 5,400,000 toman a month (about $20.35) \[D\] and lifetime value about 80.5M toman (about $303) at 6% monthly churn \[D\]. Break-even needs about 97 accounts \[D\] because fixed costs of 466.3M toman a month are large against an ARPU this low. Base-case month 24 uses 9 GPU nodes, about 62% of that month's cost of 2,194M, and 5 added support staff, about 8% \[D\]. Account counts are \[A\]: I found no count of Iranian SMEs or agencies that would pay for an agent builder. Foreign tools are the reference: Zapier Professional costs $19.99 a month for 750 tasks and $129 for 10,000 \[S, toolradar.com, updated 30 Oct 2026\], Make from $9 for 10,000 operations \[S, same page\], and n8n can be self-hosted on a $15-30 VPS \[S, same page\], so a free self-hosted alternative exists for technical buyers. A run here is not the same unit as a Zapier task, so the price comparison is only approximate \[A\]. Integrations with Iranian services (payment gateways, messengers, accounting tools) are the product's real moat and cost, and their API access was not verified.

99.title: On-premises document Q&A ("chat with your files")
99.verdict_md: Verdict: viable on the numbers, but the result rests on a small, unsourced buyer pool and a sales cycle the model does not capture. The base case (30 deployments at month 24) breaks even in month 8, peaks at a cash need of 2,882M toman (about $10,864) and reaches +25,980M toman cumulative by month 24 \[D\]. The conservative case (12 deployments) breaks even in month 14 and is +1,310M cumulative at month 24; the optimistic case (80) breaks even in month 5 and ends at +91,225M \[D\]. The sensitivities hold: a doubled GPU price breaks even in month 9, prices 30% lower in month 10, half the deployments in month 13 \[D\]. ARPU is 156,000,000 toman a month per deployment (about $588.02) \[D\] and lifetime value about 10,163M toman (about $38,307) at 1.5% monthly churn \[D\]. The margins are high because the customer buys and runs its own GPU hardware, so only a 150M toman staging node and people are our costs \[A\]; the cost lies in implementation staff, not compute. Foreign on-premises RAG builds cost $80,000 to $150,000 or more to implement plus $3,000 to $5,000 or more a month to operate \[S, thenegotiationexperts.com, updated May 2026\], against monthly plans here of about $226, $754 and $2,639 \[D\] with no implementation fee modelled \[A\]. The deployment counts are \[A\]: I found no count of Iranian banks, factories or ministries buying private LLM systems. A first run with 25 / 100 deployments gave unrealistically smooth results for an unsourced pool, so I cut the counts to 8 / 30, raised implementation staffing to 1 person per 8 deployments and marketing to 60M toman a month before reporting; those changes were made for realism, not to pass. Licence blockers: the open model's commercial licence and Persian document quality (scanned PDFs, Persian OCR) were not checked.

100.title: Persian dataset labeling and model-evaluation service
100.verdict_md: Verdict: viable on the numbers but thin-margined and labour-bound; the buyer pool is unsourced. The base case (120 paying accounts at month 24) breaks even in month 6, peaks at a cash need of 1,571M toman (about $5,921) and reaches +52,193M toman cumulative by month 24 \[D\]. The conservative case (40 accounts) breaks even in month 10 and is at +11,061M cumulative at month 24; the optimistic case (300) breaks even in month 4 and ends at +147,992M \[D\]. The sensitivities show the exposure: prices 30% lower mean no break-even within 24 months and a month-24 loss of 116M a month; a doubled GPU price still breaks even in month 6; half the accounts break even in month 8 \[D\]. ARPU is 183,200,000 toman a month (about $690.55) \[D\] and lifetime value about 851.6M toman (about $3,210) at 8% monthly churn \[D\]. Gross margins are 47.7%, 37.5% and 25.8% by plan \[D\] because annotator pay is the main cost: about 87% of base-case month-24 cost of 15,571M \[D\], against about 3% for GPU nodes and 6% for 20 added project managers \[D\]. Annotator cost is \[A\]: I priced annotators at the 1405 minimum wage loaded at 23% insurance (143,023 toman an hour \[D\]) at 60 items an hour plus 25% review, and no Iranian annotation wage or throughput was found. Account counts are \[A\]: no count of Iranian AI teams buying labelling or evaluation was found. Foreign labelling is listed at $0.05 to $2.00 per item for classification and entity tasks \[S, aisuperior.com, 17 Apr 2026\], against plan prices here of 6,000, 5,000 and 4,200 toman per item (about $0.023, $0.019 and $0.016) \[D\], so the domestic price is below the foreign range; whether Iranian buyers would pay even that, or send work abroad, is unknown. Quality risk is high: label accuracy, annotator reliability and agreement rates were not tested, and no licence issue arises beyond the buyer's own data rights.

sections_md.risks:
- Labour cost and supply: annotators are 87% of cost and priced at minimum wage and 60 items an hour \[D, A\]; higher wages or slower throughput remove the margin.

- Quality: label accuracy and agreement were not tested; a bad dataset costs the buyer more than the fee, so churn may be higher than 8%.
- Buyer pool: no count of Iranian teams buying labelling; academic buyers may have little budget \[A\].
- Substitution: buyers can label with an LLM or with their own staff; LLM-assisted labelling is cheaper per item but its quality was not measured.

verdict_blocks.x: Verdict: viable on the numbers but thin-margined and labour-bound; the buyer pool is unsourced. The base case (120 paying accounts at month 24) breaks even in month 6, peaks at a cash need of 1,571M toman (about $5,921) and reaches +52,193M toman cumulative by month 24 [D]. The conservative case (40 accounts) breaks even in month 10 and is at +11,061M cumulative at month 24; the optimistic case (300) breaks even in month 4 and ends at +147,992M [D]. The sensitivities show the exposure: prices 30% lower mean no break-even within 24 months and a month-24 loss of 116M a month; a doubled GPU price still breaks even in month 6; half the accounts break even in month 8 [D]. ARPU is 183,200,000 toman a month (about $690.55) [D] and lifetime value about 851.6M toman (about $3,210) at 8% monthly churn [D]. Gross margins are 47.7%, 37.5% and 25.8% by plan [D] because annotator pay is the main cost: about 87% of base-case month-24 cost of 15,571M [D], against about 3% for GPU nodes and 6% for 20 added project managers [D]. Annotator cost is [A]: I priced annotators at the 1405 minimum wage loaded at 23% insurance (143,023 toman an hour [D]) at 60 items an hour plus 25% review, and no Iranian annotation wage or throughput was found. Account counts are [A]: no count of Iranian AI teams buying labelling or evaluation was found. Foreign labelling is listed at $0.05 to $2.00 per item for classification and entity tasks [S, aisuperior.com, 17 Apr 2026], against plan prices here of 6,000, 5,000 and 4,200 toman per item (about $0.023, $0.019 and $0.016) [D], so the domestic price is below the foreign range; whether Iranian buyers would pay even that, or send work abroad, is unknown. Quality risk is high: label accuracy, annotator reliability and agreement rates were not tested, and no licence issue arises beyond the buyer's own data rights.
